fragments.text: Target edition: 17 October 2026. Satchel is the US small-firm practice management system a Clio Manage, MyCase, Smokeball or PracticePanther buyer can switch to, with Filevine’s matter-work depth and source-grounded assistance beyond today’s Eve workflows. It runs intake and conflicts, engagements, matters, documents and email, court deadlines, client communication, time capture, billing, built-in trust accounting, legal payments and collections.

This is the product being built towards. Missing implementation is a gap, never a reason to narrow the product. Each named clause describes buyer behavior and an acceptance journey through a public screen, route, download, command or real provider boundary. Current status is judged separately from that target. ACCEPTANCE.md lists the same journeys and statuses for build rounds. No product code, approved homepage, UI or behavior changes in this documentation round.
| Category | Legal practice management software |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Clio, MyCase (8am), Smokeball, PracticePanther; Filevine and Eve |

| First buyer | The principal or administrator of a 1–10 lawyer US firm, with lawyers, assistants, billing staff and an outside accountant; USD fees, US banks, US court practice and US client communication norms |

Satchel owns the legal practice loop from prospective client through closed matter and reconciled money. Trust accounting is built in: client subsidiary ledgers, bank registers and three-way reconciliation are core product obligations, not a link to an external spreadsheet. Banks and contracted processors hold and move actual money. Counsel retains conflict clearance, legal judgments, deadline confirmation and external filing authority. Agents prepare and act only under explicit delegated nonlegal authority; people retain legal and financial approvals.

The published foundation had no root CONTRACT.md or named clause IDs. SAT-001 through SAT-013 give stable names to its existing ACCEPTANCE.md promises, preserving the behavior. Their 1 MiB implementation limit and old exclusions of delivered invoices, trust accounting and provider calls describe the prior release, not target boundaries. New target clauses supersede those scope exclusions while preserving original-byte integrity, review history and authority checks. USD cents remain exact; foreign-currency invoices require explicit agreements and separate currency ledgers.

Neighboring products remain separate. [Chest](https://github.com/just-every/run-chest) owns general-purpose file collaboration; Satchel owns matter evidence and connects repositories. [Inkwell](https://github.com/just-every/run-inkwell) supplies signatures, alongside DocuSign; Satchel owns engagement and matter workflow. [Pantry](https://github.com/just-every/run-pantry) is a general accounting product; Satchel owns legal billing and IOLTA subsidiary accounting and connects QuickBooks Online/Xero. General CRM, enterprise e-discovery and unrestricted legal research databases remain separate products; matter intake, scoped research integration and evidence production remain Satchel obligations.

All clauses inherit server-side authorization, matter confidentiality, stable source identities, append-only posted financial records, reviewed exact revisions, durable job state and explicit uncertain outcomes. Native Base session/import/portability guarantees continue through BASE-001. A fresh production installation contains no sample clients. Examples in acceptance journeys are test inputs, never seeded production records. Paid/network services may use official sandboxes at the edge; application workflows must use real application handlers.
**SAT-001 — Invite a firm team.** The principal saves and invites lawyers and assistants, deactivates membership and controls matter grants.
Private handlers check the native session, active firm role and matter access themselves; a hidden button is never the boundary.
**Acceptance evidence:** Through Team and the JSON API invite an assistant, grant one matter, read it, then revoke membership; direct private reads and writes fail immediately.

**SAT-002 — Review fresh conflicts before opening.** A principal or lawyer searches firm parties, adverse parties and aliases, reviews recorded matches and writes a conclusion before opening a matter. Any party insert, update or delete invalidates the search; linking already-known, unchanged parties to a new matter does not. Each conflict search clears one opening only, so two separately reviewed openings that involve only existing, unchanged parties may both succeed concurrently. Search is evidence for counsel, never a guarantee of legal clearance. **Acceptance evidence:** Run a conflict search, change a party record, attempt opening against the stale search and receive refusal; repeat with fresh review and explicit confirmation to open. Open two separately reviewed matters involving only existing, unchanged parties concurrently and both succeed; reusing either search is refused.

**SAT-003 — Grant matter access.** The principal grants or removes access to individual matters. Other staff see only assigned matters; the principal can see all. Finance and ethical-wall extensions in FIRM-002 and FIRM-003 add narrower authority without claiming they exist today. Its grant door refuses staff excluded by an INTAKE-005 engagement restriction, naming it (proved under INTAKE-005). **Acceptance evidence:** As an unassigned assistant request a matter and its billing, files and deadlines directly, receive refusal, then grant and remove access and repeat.

**SAT-004 — Record exact USD work.** Authorized staff record dated matter time in whole minutes and hourly USD cents, or disbursements in USD cents. Charges use exact integer arithmetic with declared half-up rounding to cents; invalid dates and unsafe amounts are refused. **Acceptance evidence:** Record 90 minutes at $250 per hour and a $25 disbursement through Time & bills; inspect $400 in the prepared package and reject an invalid date.

**SAT-005 — Review immutable bill exports.** A lawyer prepares a bill from unbilled matter entries, reviews the exact revision and exports its recorded CSV artifact. Source reservations prevent double billing; assistants and agents cannot approve, and an exported artifact cannot be voided in place or overwritten: a later BILL-016 void is a separate append-only record beside it. **Acceptance evidence:** Reserve entries in a draft, refuse another bill using them, refuse premature export and assistant approval, approve as counsel and download the immutable CSV.

**SAT-006 — Correct by reviewed additions.** A correction is a separately reviewed delta referencing the original bill and source amounts. The original exported artifact, review identity and history remain intact. A delta adjusts an amount without releasing entries; when the entries themselves are wrong (matter, rate, narrative or template), BILL-016 voids the invoice and rebills them. **Acceptance evidence:** Create and approve a courtesy reduction through the billing API; export its negative delta and download the original again with identical bytes.
BILL-015 cutover is the principal’s first saved scheme.

fragments.text: **SAT-007 — Keep private original versions.** Matter documents retain original bytes, hashes, version metadata and creator history. Matter visibility follows access; private visibility is uploader/principal only. Downloads validate integrity and use safe attachment headers. The current implementation limit is 1 MiB; DOC-001 widens the target. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload private and matter-visible originals, refuse the assistant private download, append a version and retrieve both originals through authenticated file routes.

**SAT-008 — Confirm source-linked deadlines.** A deadline has a date, IANA timezone, source citation and optional exact document version. A lawyer confirms and completes it with evidence. A changed source version supersedes earlier live deadlines and requires fresh review. **Acceptance evidence:** Propose and confirm a cited deadline, append its source version, refuse completion of the superseded date, then confirm a replacement and record delivery evidence.

**SAT-009 — Let agents prepare for people.** Revocable agent credentials read only within their human sponsor’s access and prepare matter, bill and deadline proposals. A person approves or declines once; approving a proposal does not substitute for conflict, bill or deadline review. **Acceptance evidence:** Use an agent key to prepare each proposal, refuse agent approval and repeated human decisions, check the human decision record, then revoke the key and refuse access.

**SAT-010 — Preview Clio contact move-in.** The principal previews the documented Clio contacts CSV through Base import-kit, commits its exact fingerprint, resumes and inspects the provenance journal. Replay reuses the job; undo removes unchanged unused contacts and preserves native matter links. Full Clio migration is MOVE-002. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload fixtures/clio-contacts.csv through Move in, prove preview writes nothing, refuse a changed fingerprint, apply and replay, open a linked matter and undo while preserving its contact.
**SAT-011 — Restore a private firm archive.**
The principal exports the complete current native firm archive and restores only into empty product data after integrity validation.

Product records, review history and import provenance round-trip; identity, sessions, local configuration and agent keys remain excluded. **Acceptance evidence:** Export through Team & safety, refuse corrupt and nonempty restore, restore into an empty installation, export again and compare all native rows and original bill bytes.

fragments.text: **SAT-012 — Erase originals with a restore fence.** A principal confirms a document name and reason to erase every version’s bytes while preserving metadata, hashes and the erasure journal. Supplying the later journal fences older archives; copies already downloaded or delivered remain outside local erasure. **Acceptance evidence:** Erase through the document API, refuse assistant erasure, confirm all version downloads fail and reject a pre-erasure backup when accompanied by the later journal.

**SAT-013 — Keep the chosen product surfaces.** The public site retains Run Satchel at /run and navigable Markdown guides at /docs. The installed root remains the Lobby; sign-in, setup and all workspace tabs retain the picked theme and available actions at desktop and phone widths. **Acceptance evidence:** Navigate the built site’s run instructions and guides; at 1440 and 390 pixels complete sign-in, setup and each workspace tab with real matter records, checking actions and role restrictions.
**OSS-001 — Free and open source, MIT licensed.** Satchel’s source is publicly available under the MIT license, with no Satchel license fee, subscription, paywall, seat charge or matter limit.
A firm runs it on its own computer or server, including its own Cloudflare account.

Payment, e-signature and accounting providers, including LawPay, Stripe, DocuSign, Inkwell, QuickBooks Online and Xero, bill the firm directly under their own terms, as do hosting, mail, SMS, court-rule and filing providers; “100% free” describes Satchel software, not those provider services. **Acceptance evidence:** Read `LICENSE` and the homepage, /run, README and owner guides and verify they agree on MIT, free Satchel software, self-hosting and direct provider billing. Follow the published run command on a fresh installation and complete the native matter/time/bill workflow without any Satchel payment, plan or license prompt. Before connecting a provider inspect its terms and direct firm-billing disclosure and prove Satchel adds no software or provider-resale charge.

**FIRM-001 — Set up an empty US firm.** A fresh installation starts with the buyer’s firm, offices, US contact details, practice areas, IANA timezone, USD billing defaults and fiscal settings entered by the principal or imported with provenance: imported from a Satchel firm-settings JSON file (the one **Download firm settings** produces), recorded with its file name and SHA-256; a full firm archive restore also carries the settings and their provenance. Importing firm settings from Clio, MyCase and other products belongs to MOVE-002 to MOVE-007. Production never starts with demo clients. **Acceptance evidence:** Start a fresh installation, finish setup, inspect empty matters and enter firm settings; download them and import the file into a fresh installation, where the source shows its file name and SHA-256; restore a full firm archive and find the same settings and provenance.

**FIRM-002 — Separate finance and legal rights.** Principal manages membership and policies; lawyers clear conflicts, confirm legal deadlines and approve legal work; assistants manage assigned work without legal approval; billing staff draft and deliver approved bills; trust officers authorize transfers; accountants reconcile with read-only matter context; clients see explicit portal grants. **Roles and client sharing (ct approved 22 October 2026).**

Billing staff draft bills and, once a lawyer or the principal has approved one, issue and export it; they cannot approve, reach trust records, conflicts, membership or matter access. Accountants read their assigned matters, billing and every trust record and reconcile (import a statement period, record bank clearance, match checks) but cannot authorize, sign or reopen a period or change anything else. A client reaches no staff door: only the principal shares one matter at a time with an active client member, with a recorded reason and an audit entry, and the client then sees that matter’s number, title and status; a walled matter is never shown and withdrawing the share closes the view. Agent keys and integrations need a principal, lawyer, assistant or trust-officer sponsor, so a member whose role changes to billing, accountant or client loses any earlier key at once. FIRM-008’s custom roles narrow these roles and never widen them; CLIENT-001 to CLIENT-009 own portal identities, content and messaging beyond this view and inherit the share and withdrawal rules.

**Acceptance evidence:** Create each role and use direct APIs for legal approval, invoice delivery, trust transfer, reconciliation and access changes; deny every capability outside that role. Also: as billing staff draft and issue an approved bill but fail to approve it; as an accountant reconcile and fail to authorize, sign or change a matter; as a client see only a shared matter, with every staff door refused.

**FIRM-003 — Enforce ethical walls.** Restricted matters support explicit ethical walls, excluding ordinary administrators and search, exports, notifications, connected repositories and agent context. A designated custodian records exceptional access with reason and an audit entry. Before shipping, inherit REPORT-001’s exclusion of a principal outside the wall from every report row, count, drill, option and CSV. The principal establishes a wall with an active lawyer or principal custodian and explicit members; subsequent membership changes belong only to the custodian. Exceptional access requires the custodian’s recorded reason, expires within 60 minutes, can be revoked and never delegates to agents or integrations. Membership changes revoke outstanding exceptional grants. Current matter doors, search, reports, notifications and exports intersect wall access; an indivisible firm archive, import original or account aggregate is refused unless every included wall permits the reader. DOC-010, DOC-011 and DOC-014 inherit the same boundary before connected repositories or desktop caches ship. **Wall authority (ct 22 Oct 2026).**

The principal establishes a wall naming an active lawyer or principal custodian, who is always a wall member; for a wall INTAKE-010 creates at opening, the default custodian is the lawyer who records the restriction. After creation only the current custodian changes membership, hands custodianship to another active lawyer or principal inside the wall, or dissolves the wall, each with a recorded reason; nobody outside the wall, the principal and administrators included, adds themselves, changes members or custodian, approves access or dissolves it. With no active custodian the wall stays in force, reads "custodian unassigned", allows no exceptional access, and an active lawyer or principal inside the wall may take custodianship with a recorded reason. Exceptional access is requested with a reason by one active person in a native session (never an agent key, integration, portal user or client contact). Only the current custodian approves or refuses it, with a decision note. It lasts at most 60 minutes from approval and never renews: a further need is a new request. It is revoked early by the custodian or by any membership or custodian change. It opens the walled matter's current doors for that person only. It never confers membership or custodian authority, never reaches their agent keys or integrations, and never counts toward the every-wall permission for whole-firm archives, import originals or account aggregates. Request, decision, expiry, revocation and the recipient's walled reads under a grant are FIRM-005 audit actions readable inside the wall; the recipient sees their own request, decision and expiry. INTAKE-010's walled routing and the walls its restrictions create are proved under INTAKE-010.

**Acceptance evidence:** Wall off an adverse matter, search and export as a principal outside the wall, then approve a documented emergency access and inspect its trace. Also (ct 22 Oct 2026): as the principal outside the wall, be refused adding yourself, changing members, re-designating the custodian, dissolving the wall and approving your own request; as an agent key and an integration, be refused requesting or using exceptional access. As the custodian, approve the principal's request, see it refused after 60 minutes, approve another and see it revoked by a membership change and again by handing custodianship to an inside lawyer. Under an active grant, be refused a whole-firm archive. Deactivate the custodian and see "custodian unassigned" with no grant possible until an inside lawyer takes custodianship.
**FIRM-004 — Secure sessions and connected secrets.**

Native sign-in is extended with MFA or federated SSO, session/device revocation and least-privilege connector grants. Current outbound data declaration: CONNECT-001 lets only the principal explicitly enable a public HTTPS webhook destination and selected matter metadata events (stable matter/record/event IDs, type and time; no original bytes or private titles). Its Worker fetch refuses credentials, fragments, reserved names, non-public literal addresses and redirects; there is no separate DNS preflight or application address pin. Resolved-address/pinned egress (Base egress door) is inherited here by name and keeps CONNECT-001 partial until adopted. Secrets stay installation-local, encrypted at rest, redacted from logs and absent from archives; revocation stops new work and exposes in-flight uncertainty.
**Acceptance evidence:** Sign in with MFA, revoke a device and a Microsoft connector while work is queued, then attempt reads and inspect logs and an export.

FIRM-004 implementation semantics: Native email sign-in requires a security passphrase and time-based authenticator code on each new session after the person explicitly enrolls; codes cannot replay across sessions, attempts are limited and device revocation uses the native session fence. The principal reviews Microsoft terms and explicitly approves only directory reads using installation-local Entra application credentials. The fixed Graph endpoint returns only directory IDs and display names on a fresh authorized execution; its durable journal retains counts and safe outcomes. Entra administrators must grant only User.Read.All; Satchel's fixed operation cannot narrow independently granted application permissions. Revocation wipes the encrypted token cache, refuses queued reads and labels already claimed work uncertain. Current originating session and connector generation are checked before the request and before releasing its response. Authenticator seeds, salted passphrase hashes, session confirmations, connector credentials and credential-bound queues are excluded from archives; safe audit history remains. These conservative defaults await ct approval.

**FIRM-005 — Export a complete action audit.** Authorized custodians filter and export an append-only history of actor, role, matter, source, revision, human decision, automation policy and provider outcome. Audit access respects walls; corrections add records rather than rewriting prior actions. The principal is the current native custodian. Every capability and provider that exists today records this evidence; FIRM-002, FIRM-003, FIRM-004, FIRM-008, BILL-005/006/007, BOOKS-001/002, CONNECT-003 and AGENT-010 inherit the obligation before their new roles, walls, providers, policies or doors ship, as does each future clause adding a capability or record kind. Legacy rows retain every original field unchanged; unavailable role, channel, source and revision fields remain null and are labeled “legacy, not recorded”, never inferred from present membership. Audit date filters include whole UTC calendar days, ordered by action timestamp and ID. Export streams a frozen append-only snapshot with its record count; its own export-request action is recorded after that snapshot. Archive restore retains all imported rows unchanged and appends a new custody action naming the exact supplied archive hash. **Acceptance evidence:** Open the audit, filter a matter and date range, export a transfer and approval trail, and verify an unauthorized reader cannot inspect it.

**FIRM-006 — Apply retention and legal holds.** Counsel (the principal or a lawyer on the matter) places and releases legal holds and sets matter and document retention schedules; holds block scheduled disposal and ordinary erasure. Until FIRM-002 and FIRM-008 define a custodian role, expiration asks the principal, who approves disposal. Approved disposal removes originals and every derivative, and its journal counts each kind removed: today Satchel keeps no previews, OCR text, search vectors or connector caches, so the journal records zero of each; when DOC-002 (previews), DOC-003 (OCR and search index) and DOC-010 (connector caches) add derivatives, disposal must remove them and the journal must count them. DOC-002’s separate annotations and retained conflict originals are also removed and counted individually. DOC-012 chronology snapshots and reviews and DOC-013 production packets and manifests are removed when any source is disposed, and the journal counts affected chronologies and productions. Before a lead-retention door ships, FIRM-006 must also apply its holds, disposal, original and derivative removal and restore-fence obligations to INTAKE-001 inquiry records and R2 originals. A disposed document keeps only a tombstone (name, erasure time and journal) in its matter’s document list: no download returns any version, and no document search, saved view search or duplicate check finds it. INTAKE-005 waivers and restriction records are retained conflict originals. **Acceptance evidence:** As a lawyer on the matter place a hold, request erasure and receive a refusal; release it, let the schedule expire and approve disposal as the principal (a lawyer or assistant cannot approve it); prove all downloads and searches stop and the disposal journal counts every derivative kind removed (zero previews, OCR text, search vectors and connector caches today).

**FIRM-007 — Operate and recover the owned system.** The principal owns deployment and provider accounts, sees storage/connector costs and health diagnostics that name each connector’s authorization and token expiry, last successful sync, queued and failed jobs, scheduled-job lag, storage use against quota, last verified backup and restore test, bank-feed staleness and unreconciled trust periods, each with its next action. The principal exports full archives with large attachments and reconciled trust history. Restore validates counts and hashes, keeps secrets local and leaves external sending and charging paused until reauthorized. **Acceptance evidence:** Restore a populated target firm into a new installation, reconcile attachment hashes and trust totals, expire a connector token and stop the bank feed and see each named in diagnostics with its next action, and prove no imported job sends or charges. On a fresh computer run `npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-satchel`, reach the local installation, then follow the owner deployment guide to run it in the firm’s own server/Cloudflare account without a Satchel subscription.

**FIRM-008 — Define custom roles and rate visibility.** Beyond FIRM-002’s built-in roles, the principal defines custom roles with per-area permissions: billing rates (none, own, all), operating and trust bank accounts (none, balances only, full transactions), reports (none, own matters, firm-wide), contacts, documents, billing and settings.
Server-side handlers apply the role to every read, export, search result and report; a role change takes effect on the next request and is audited.

Legal approval and trust authorization stay tied to FIRM-002’s lawyer and trust-officer authority, and a custom role cannot confer them. Before shipping, apply those report scopes to every REPORT-001 row, count, drill and CSV. **Exact semantics.** A custom role is a named ceiling the principal places on one active member who is not a client or the principal, beside their built-in role: it lowers what that role could reach and never raises it, so legal approval, conflict clearance, trust authorization, matter grants and ethical walls stay exactly as FIRM-002 and FIRM-003 define them, and a role that names trust authorization or legal approval is refused. Rates: none, own (entries, drafts and bill lines the member recorded, plus agreements naming no timekeeper) or all; every other timekeeper’s rate, amount and discount, and every frozen CSV, LEDES or XML text, is withheld and marked, never shown as zero, while bill totals remain, and exports that carry rates need all. Bank: none, balances (account and subsidiary-ledger balances only) or full; a bill row shows no trust custody without full. Reports: none, own (matters whose responsible attorney is the member and leads assigned to them, applied before every row, count, drill, option and CSV) or firm-wide, always inside current grants and walls. Contacts, documents, billing and settings: none, read (reads only) or write (the built-in role decides). Every server door of a session, an agent key and its proposals, and an integration key is assigned to its areas in one map the principal can read, and a door missing from it is refused to a narrowed member.
A change applies at the next request; the audit keeps actor, role, previous permissions and each assignment.

FIRM-004, DOC-010, DOC-011, DOC-014, REPORT-002, REPORT-003, BOOKS-001, BOOKS-002, BILL-005 to BILL-016 and every new door inherit the map: each must be given an area before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a role with own-rate visibility and no trust bank access and assign it to an assistant; request another timekeeper’s rate through the timesheet, draft invoice, report and export routes and the IOLTA register directly and receive refusal or redaction; widen the role, repeat, and inspect the audit of both changes; refuse a custom role that grants trust authorization.

**BASE-001 — Preserve Base guarantees through replacements.** Satchel retains native Base identity, imports, portability and erasure guarantees. Its custom archive/erase doors replace generic product export/erasure for matter records, including originals, review history, import journals and erasure fences; this replacement must grow with every new product record. **Acceptance evidence:** Through native sign-in and Satchel backup, restore and erasure routes round-trip every native record, omit local authority and refuse stale erased content.

**INTAKE-001 — Publish conditional intake forms.** Staff publish branded accessible forms with conditional questions, consent, secure attachments, spam controls and practice-specific fields. Every submission becomes a permissioned lead with source and receipt; sensitive replies never appear in public URLs or notification subjects. The principal and lawyers publish immutable numbered form versions with the firm name, optional PNG/JPEG logo, practice label, plain-text review consent and typed text, choice, date or yes/no questions. A conditional question depends on one earlier choice or yes/no answer; the server refuses hidden answers and validates required visible answers. Publication names an active principal, lawyer or assistant as the lead assignee. A submission requires explicit consent for receipt and review of that inquiry only: it never matches a contact identity, changes channel consent or authorizes sending. The public page uses strict-origin referrers and exact-origin submissions; a random, hashed 20-minute token binds the published revision, a honeypot and at most ten accepted submissions per form/network/UTC hour limit spam. Only an hourly HMAC network digest is retained, for at most two hours; scheduled cleanup removes expired security data. One accepted submission atomically records one native lead, source form/version, immutable answers and consent evidence, original-file references and an opaque receipt; replay returns the same receipt, never a second lead. The receipt is displayed after POST, with no anonymous read-back page, email or notification. At most three PDF, PNG or JPEG originals of up to 10 MiB each (10,485,760 bytes) are stored in R2 after byte-signature/type checks; they are labeled not malware-scanned, never rendered inline, and authenticated attachment downloads verify their hashes. Each private read and download applies INTAKE-002 visibility to both the original lead and every survivor after a merge; merging never grants the survivor assignee access to an invisible source original. R2 originals and immutable provenance round-trip in streamed native archives; credentials, spent tokens, network digests and temporary upload reservations do not. Interrupted upload reservations expire after twenty minutes for cleanup; current uploads ask an archive request to wait rather than exporting incomplete originals. INTAKE-007 inherits complete inquiry provenance and the prohibition on sensitive URL/notification-subject content; DOC-001 carries larger/resumable uploads and quarantine, while FIRM-006 must add lead-original retention, holds, disposal and restore fencing before its lead-retention door ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit a family-law inquiry with a conditional answer and attachment from a phone; inspect the private lead, receipt and consent history.

**INTAKE-002 — Manage a lead pipeline.** Staff qualify, assign and move leads through editable stages, keep referral source, consultation outcome and next action, detect duplicates and report stalled or lost leads with reasons. Staff record a lead with the prospect’s name, optional email and phone, inquiry summary and referral source; the referral source and creator are fixed provenance. Until INTAKE-001 forms ship, staff record leads by hand; each INTAKE-001 submission must become one of these leads before it ships. The principal and lawyers see and maintain every lead and configure the ordered pipeline stages; an assistant sees and works only leads assigned to them, records new leads assigned to themselves and cannot reassign or merge; trust officers see no leads. Assignees are active lawyers, assistants or the principal. A lead is qualified (pending, qualified or not qualified), moved between stages, and keeps a consultation outcome and a next action with an optional date. Each change is checked against the lead’s revision and appended to its immutable history. A possible duplicate is another open lead with the same email (case-insensitive), the same phone digits (at least seven) or the same name (ignoring case and spacing). Counsel merges a duplicate into a surviving lead: the survivor keeps its own fields, and the duplicate stays as a merged record with its source, referral, creator and history, shown as the survivor’s provenance. Losing a lead requires a reason. Converting links a matter opened through the conflict-reviewed door that the person can see, one lead per matter; INTAKE-007 adds full carry-over and MATTER-004’s opening trigger applies to that matter. Each person’s due queue lists their own open leads whose next-action date is on or before the firm-local today, flagged overdue when it is earlier. An open lead is stalled when its next action is overdue or when its last activity was 14 or more firm-local calendar days ago (inclusive). A missing next-action date alone is not stalled. Lead names and details never appear in notification subjects; INTAKE-001, INTAKE-007 and every future lead notification door inherit this rule before shipping. The conversion report excludes merged duplicates and counts leads, open, converted and lost leads by referral source and by stage, with conversion shown as converted ÷ leads in whole percent, rounded half-up. It lists stalled leads with their reasons and lost leads with their recorded reasons, and each person’s report covers only the leads they can see. **Acceptance evidence:** Assign two prospects, merge a duplicate with preserved provenance, miss a follow-up and inspect the owner’s due queue and conversion report.

**INTAKE-003 — Book consultations.** Prospects book approved availability with timezone conversion, buffers, fees if required, reminders and reschedule/cancel links; consultation records and intake answers reach the responsible lawyer without duplicate calendar bookings. **Acceptance evidence:** Book the last available slot, race a second booking, reschedule across timezones and verify one appointment and the linked intake record.

**INTAKE-004 — Maintain a legal contact graph.** People and organizations have aliases, former names, related entities, addresses, communication consent and matter roles such as client, adverse party, insurer, witness, expert and counsel. Deduplication preserves relationships and conflict history. The principal or a lawyer maintains the graph; assistants and trust officers read only contacts attached to permitted matters, with only permitted matter-role links. Firm contact access does not grant matter detail. Stable source party IDs and import provenance remain separate from the surviving contact ID. A person explicitly classifies both contacts, chooses a same-kind survivor and records a reason; a recorded exact preview binds that person, role and graph revision and applies once. Every physical source ID, profile, alias, former name, address, related-entity link, matter role and recorded conflict snapshot remains intact; a losing ID resolves to its survivor, without rewriting historical matter or financial text. Consent evidence is append-only per source identity and channel (email, phone, SMS and post), unknown by default. The latest recorded decision for each identity controls, in durable recording order; the entered evidence date is an attestation, not a scheduled change. Any denied identity makes the merged channel denied; otherwise all identities must allow or it stays unknown. A merge grants no messaging or sync authority: INTAKE-008, INTAKE-009, CLIENT-005 and CLIENT-006 must enforce their own current authority before shipping their new doors. **Acceptance evidence:** Import two aliases of an insurer, relate it to two matters, merge the duplicate and search every relationship without losing source identities.

**INTAKE-005 — Review conflicts across the whole firm.** Conflict review searches former and prospective clients, related entities, aliases, staff relationships and closed matters; it records possible matches, counsel’s disposition, waivers and engagement restrictions without exposing walled detail to unauthorized people. Search evidence records the number of canonical contacts actually scanned and all physical source identities, including merged identities. An explicit client role on a permitted open matter is labeled current client; on a permitted closed matter it is labeled former client, with the year of that matter’s current closure event in the firm IANA timezone (UTC before setup). These are recorded matter associations, not a determination that professional duties ended. The search retains those counts, timezone and associations at review time; reopening does not rewrite them, and later reads reapply current matter grants. Earlier search counts remain unrecorded, never inferred. **Classifications, waivers, restrictions and restricted routing (ct 22 Oct 2026).**

Only the principal and lawyers (SAT-002, FIRM-002) search, dispose, record waivers and set engagement restrictions; assistants, trust officers, agents and portal users cannot. Besides current and former clients, matches are labelled *prospective client* for a contact on a lead (INTAKE-002) or consultation (INTAKE-003) not converted, with its stage and firm-local year; *related entity* through INTAKE-004 links; and *staff relationship* for a relationship the principal or a lawyer recorded between a staff member and a contact (kind, dates, source), shown to the principal and lawyers only. Labels are recorded associations, never determinations. A match whose matter role the searcher cannot read under current grants or private-record rules is a *restricted match*: the searcher sees the matched contact and alias as INTAKE-004 allows and, in place of every hidden matter, role, title and count, one route per custodian ("Restricted match: routed to <custodian>"). Until FIRM-003 ships the custodian is the principal, the current native custodian (FIRM-005, FIRM-006). The custodian records a disposition from a closed set (no conflict; waivable, waiver recorded; proceed with engagement restrictions; decline) bound to that review's revision; the searcher sees only the outcome, custodian, time and any restriction text the custodian writes for disclosure. Opening is refused until every route has a current custodian disposition, no route says decline, every waivable match has a waiver and counsel's overall disposition is recorded; any party change makes all of them stale (SAT-002). A waiver records the waiving contacts (each holding a client role on the affected matter), date, scope text and the match it answers, with a file or a written confirmation, labelled "practitioner-recorded, not signed through Satchel" until INTAKE-006 supplies signatures; a restricted match's waiver is recorded and read only by its custodian. Engagement restrictions attach to the new matter at opening: disclosed condition text on the matter header for everyone with access, and excluded non-principal staff whom SAT-003's grant door refuses, naming the restriction; removing one needs the principal or a lawyer on the matter with a reason. Every route, disposition, waiver and restriction is a FIRM-005 audit action, travels in archives, and is retained, held and disposed with FIRM-006's retained conflict originals. Retained restriction payload disposal uses FIRM-006: the principal types the search reference and records a reason, every affected source and opened matter has an expired schedule and no hold, and saved counsel notes, condition text, acknowledgment text and their audit payload copies are replaced by a disposal marker. Stable ids, decisions, attribution, times and original audit digests remain. Existing staff exclusions and walls stay enforced; a disposed review cannot clear an engagement or accept a new disposition. New searches are required. Search, routing and disposition are evidence for counsel, never legal clearance; applying the conflict rules is the firm's.

**Acceptance evidence:** Search a former client’s alias and a prospective adverse affiliate, route a restricted match to its custodian and require recorded counsel disposition before engagement. Search across all firm contacts, imported aliases and open and closed matters, inspect the searched-contact count and a former-client match showing its matter’s closed year, and record the partner’s clearance; no contact may be silently skipped, and a restricted match reveals only its custodian route.

**INTAKE-010 — Route walled conflict matches to wall custodians.** When FIRM-003 ships, a match on a walled matter is a restricted match for everyone outside that wall, the principal and administrators included, and routes to the custodian FIRM-003 designates for that wall: a principal or lawyer inside it (default: the lawyer who created it), never a person outside it. Only that custodian disposes of the walled match, records and reads its waiver and writes its disclosed restriction text. A principal outside the wall sees only the route, outcome, custodian and time; cannot dispose, override, re-designate the custodian or add themselves to the wall; and reaches walled detail only through FIRM-003's recorded exceptional access. A contact whose only matter roles are walled shows outside the wall only as the route; its other roles show normally. With no active custodian inside the wall the route reads "custodian unassigned: ask the wall's counsel" and opening is refused. An engagement restriction that excludes the principal or requires a screen creates a FIRM-003 wall at opening naming the excluded people. Walled conflict evidence (routes, dispositions, waivers, restriction detail) stays out of search, exports, notifications, connected repositories, agent context, reports and FIRM-005 audit reads for everyone outside the wall. **Acceptance evidence:** Wall off an adverse matter with a lawyer custodian inside and the principal outside. As the principal, search the adverse party's alias and see only the route; be refused opening, disposing, re-designating the custodian and adding yourself. As the custodian, dispose with a waiver, then open. As the principal, check search, export, notifications, agent context, reports and the audit for walled detail and find none; approve an exceptional access under FIRM-003 and inspect its trace.

**INTAKE-006 — Execute engagement agreements.** Counsel selects a versioned fee agreement, reviews client and payer details, requests electronic signatures through DocuSign or Inkwell, tracks signer identity, decline/expiry and completion, and files the signed document and certificate with the matter. Before shipping, enforce INTAKE-005 and INTAKE-010’s current counsel and custodian dispositions, waivers and enforced engagement-restriction gates. Before shipping, signed waivers may come through its signature flow; practitioner-recorded INTAKE-005 waivers keep their label. **Acceptance evidence:** Send an hourly engagement to two signers, receive a signed webhook twice and inspect one completed agreement and certificate; a declined agreement cannot open an engaged matter. Inspect the approved hourly rates in the exact signed engagement, verify that one of two signatures leaves it pending and that two of two completes it with both signer identities.

**INTAKE-007 — Convert a lead without losing history.** An authorized lawyer converts a cleared, accepted engagement into a matter, carrying parties, signed terms, files, consultation notes, assigned staff and approved retainer request; idempotent conversion never opens a second matter. Before shipping, INTAKE-007 carries INTAKE-001’s exact form versions, answers, receipt and review consent, and R2 originals under the original and surviving lead access checks. Before shipping, enforce INTAKE-005 and INTAKE-010’s current counsel and custodian dispositions, waivers and enforced engagement-restriction gates. **Acceptance evidence:** Convert a signed lead twice through intake and inspect one matter with complete linked history and an uncharged retainer request. INTAKE-007 inherits INTAKE-002’s lead visibility, counsel merge, firm-local stalled-lead rules and the prohibition on lead names/details in notification subjects before shipping.

**INTAKE-008 — Follow up prospects under consent.** Owners configure consultation reminders, unanswered-inquiry follow-ups and engagement chases by channel, quiet hours and contact limits. A reply, opt-out, conflict stop or decline halts the sequence and assigns the next human action. Before this capability ships, enforce its own recorded sending or sync authority and INTAKE-004’s merged-identity consent obligations; a contact merge supplies neither authority nor consent. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule a consented lead sequence, receive a reply after its first reminder, restart the worker and verify later sends stop and responsibility remains visible.

**INTAKE-009 — Synchronize Google and Microsoft 365 contacts.** Each staff member may connect Google Contacts or Microsoft 365/Outlook contacts for two-way sync of the INTAKE-004 contacts they choose by matter role, tag or practice group, with stable remote IDs, mapping of names, organizations, emails, phones and addresses, loop prevention and a visible conflict queue. Walled, restricted and prospective-client contacts never leave Satchel unless firm policy allows; a remote edit is a proposed change, a remote delete never deletes a Satchel contact or its conflict history, and disconnecting stops sync with visible state. Before this capability ships, enforce its own recorded sending or sync authority and INTAKE-004’s merged-identity consent obligations; a contact merge supplies neither authority nor consent. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect one staff member’s Google contacts and another’s Microsoft 365 contacts, sync a client group both ways, edit one phone number in each system concurrently and resolve the conflict in the queue; delete a synced contact remotely and confirm the Satchel contact and its conflict history remain; confirm a walled matter’s adverse party never syncs; replay sync without duplicates, then disconnect and see the stopped state.

**MATTER-001 — Model practice-specific matters.** Each practice area has editable matter types, custom typed fields, case numbers, courts, opponents, insurance limits, fee arrangements and required records. Changes are versioned and validated without rewriting historic closed matters. The principal defines each matter type for one configured practice area, acting for the firm administrator until FIRM-008 custom roles exist; every save writes an immutable numbered version. Standard fields are case number, court, insurance limit (exact USD cents from at most two decimals, never rounded) and fee arrangement (hourly, flat fee, contingency, hybrid or pro bono, with optional terms); opponents are the matter’s conflict-reviewed adverse parties (SAT-002). A type marks which standard fields are required and adds typed custom fields (text, number, YYYY-MM-DD date, USD money, choice, yes/no) and required record types. The principal or a lawyer who sees the matter records values; assistants read only. Values are validated against the type version the matter adopted: a new version reaches an open matter only when counsel explicitly adopts it and every required and typed value passes, and a closed matter (MATTER-007) keeps its recorded version and values and cannot adopt another until reopened. A required record is on file when an available current original of exactly that document type is visible to the viewer, otherwise missing; it does not block saving. The matter docket shows court, case number, opponents and each visible deadline with its date, IANA timezone, status (proposed dates labeled unconfirmed), citation and exact source-document version. The Clio matters import records a case_number column with its source provenance. MOVE-002 imports, MATTER-004 workflows, DOC-006 templates and MATTER-009 search inherit the typed fields and the adopted-version rule before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Create litigation and estate templates, require different fields, import a case number and reject an invalid typed value. Set a litigation matter’s court and case number, open its docket and a confirmed deadline’s scheduling-order paragraph, and verify the displayed court, date, timezone and exact source-version citation agree.

**MATTER-002 — Track stages and milestones.** Lists and kanban boards filter matters by lawyer, practice, stage, risk and next milestone. Stage transitions enforce required evidence and show blocked or overdue work without concealing exceptions. The principal and lawyers configure named stages with required document types and update the responsible lawyer, risk (low, medium, high or urgent), next milestone and optional date on matters they may see; assistants read only. The responsible lawyer must be active and already see the matter; assignment grants no access. Both list and kanban use the same permissioned filters: lawyer, practice and stage match exactly, risk matches its label, and next milestone matches text without case. A stage transition requires a reason, the current stage-configuration and matter-profile revisions, and explicitly selected current, retained originals matching every required type exactly; their versions and SHA-256 digests are retained in the activity record. Missing or changed evidence refuses the move and records the blocker. Open, blocked and overdue work remains visible and is never completed or rescheduled by a stage move; a date is overdue strictly before today in the firm timezone (UTC before firm setup). Stage configuration changes affect future decisions; previous decisions retain their exact requirements and evidence. MATTER-004 inherits these stage checks before workflow transitions ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Move a matter to demand-ready with a missing medical bill, see the blocker, attach the bill and complete the transition with an activity record.

**MATTER-003 — Assign dependent work.** Tasks have owners, due dates, priorities, subtasks, dependencies, recurring schedules and completion evidence. Reassignment, absence coverage and bulk updates preserve history and do not silently change confirmed legal dates. The principal, lawyers and assistants who see the matter add and change tasks; an owner must be active staff who already sees the matter, and assignment grants no access. A task either has its own due date or is tied to a legal deadline and always shows that deadline’s date; tasks never change a deadline. Open prerequisites and open subtasks block completion, which requires written evidence and is final. A recurring task (daily, weekly or monthly, a monthly date clamped to the month’s last day) creates its next occurrence, with the same owner, when it is completed. A task whose owner is absent (CAL-008) on its due date, or today when later, shows that absence and any coverage until it is reassigned. Reassignment and bulk changes of owner, priority or due-date shift append per-task history with a reason; a bulk date shift skips tasks tied to a legal date and lists them. Notifications are in-app only: a new owner is told of an assignment, and when a prerequisite is completed each dependent task’s owner is told whether it is ready or what still blocks it; email and push notices belong to CAL-011 and MOBILE-002, which inherit these events before they ship, as do MATTER-004 (workflow-generated tasks), MATTER-006 (handoffs) and MATTER-007 (closure checks). **Acceptance evidence:** Assign dependent discovery tasks, reassign an absent assistant, complete a prerequisite and inspect remaining blockers and notifications.

**MATTER-004 — Run editable matter workflows.** A versioned practice workflow inherits MATTER-002’s current stage-evidence checks before approved transitions ship and generates tasks, events, document requests and draft documents from intake or approved stage transitions. The firm previews changes, chooses which open matters receive them and can stop a run without deleting completed work. Before shipping, each generated workflow run participates in MATTER-007’s live closure checks; reopening resumes a run only on its explicit counsel approval. Workflows are firm templates with immutable numbered versions of 1–50 keyed steps: a task (with priority); an appointment at a 24-hour start time and duration in the firm timezone, inviting nobody; a document request, which Satchel records and never sends; or a draft document, matter-visible plain text with the client, matter title and matter number merged. Each step is dated a whole number of days after the firm-local date it is generated. The principal or a lawyer creates and versions templates; every staff member can read them. A run starts when counsel (the principal or a lawyer who sees the matter) previews a version on the matter and approves selected steps. Triggers only propose a run for counsel’s review: a matter opened natively after its conflict review (the end of intake; imported matters propose nothing) or a MATTER-002 stage transition that has already passed its evidence checks. Workflows never move a stage themselves. Each approved step generates its record exactly once per run, so repeated approvals, restarts and rollouts create nothing twice. Stopping a run deletes and cancels nothing; restarting generates only approved steps not yet generated. A new version changes no run or generated record. The rollout preview lists the open matters the person sees whose live run uses an older version, with the steps (by key) the new version adds; only the matters counsel chooses move to it and generate those steps. Proposed and active runs and open document requests are MATTER-007 closure checks, and a closed matter generates nothing. On reopening, a live run resumes only when counsel selects it; every other live run is stopped with the reason ‘Not resumed on reopening’ and keeps what it generated. INTAKE-002’s lead conversion inherits the opening trigger, and every later step kind or trigger inherits once-only generation and these closure and reopening checks before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Preview a litigation workflow on an existing matter, approve selected steps, restart and verify each step is created once; edit the template without changing completed history.

**MATTER-005 — Keep a complete matter timeline.** Matter notes, calls, email, documents, tasks, deadlines, client commitments, bills and payments appear in a filterable chronology with source links and scoped mentions. Private notes remain excluded from client views and unauthorized search. **Acceptance evidence:** Add a private strategy note and shared progress note, file an email and inspect lawyer and client timelines for the correct entries.

**MATTER-006 — Manage staff capacity and handoff.** Supervisors see assigned workload, due work, absence coverage and unowned matters; a handoff transfers selected responsibilities with acknowledgment while preserving original timekeeper attribution and access policy. Until FIRM-002 and FIRM-008 define a supervisor role, the principal is the supervisor. The workload view lists each active staff member’s open tasks and deadline ownerships, the overdue ones and those due soon (overdue or due within 14 days of today in the firm’s timezone, inclusive), current and future absences with coverage (CAL-008) and handoffs awaiting acknowledgment; it also lists imminent work with no active owner and unowned matters (open work but no active person owning any of it). A handoff moves the selected person’s open task and deadline ownerships on chosen matters to a receiver who must already see every chosen matter; it grants no access, records per-item history, notifies the receiver in-app and stays awaiting acknowledgment until the receiver acknowledges it once. Time entries, completed tasks and their attribution never change. FIRM-002 and FIRM-008 (supervisor roles), MATTER-004 and MATTER-007 inherit these workload and handoff obligations before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Hand off an absent lawyer’s active matters, acknowledge the assignment and confirm every imminent task has an owner with no change to historic time entries.

**MATTER-007 — Close and reopen matters deliberately.** Closure checks unfinished deadlines, client promises, final bills, trust balances and original-file return; counsel resolves or explicitly carries exceptions. Reopening records its reason and restores only approved workflows and access. The principal or a lawyer who sees the matter prepares an attributed exact closure preview. Every open task, proposed or confirmed legal date, unacknowledged handoff, unbilled billable entry (nonbillable time, billable=0 under TIME-001, is recorded but never billed and is not checked), draft bill, unpaid or credited invoice branch, nonzero trust ledger and pending trust action is checked; balances use exact USD cents. Counsel also reviews a manual client-promise inventory, with retained source evidence for fulfilled promises, and records whether originals were returned (with retained confirmation), are not held, or remain outstanding. Every unresolved item needs its own carry reason, or must be resolved before a fresh preview. Changed work, finance, source originals or access invalidate the preview, and it applies only for its preparing person and once. Closure is a recorded disposition, not a write ban: no task, reminder, appointment or handoff is canceled, no access is revoked, and all carried ownership and due obligations continue. Reopening requires a reason and explicit selections of retained tasks, deadlines, appointments, reminders and existing access; empty selections are allowed, no jobs start and no grants change implicitly. Full immutable close/reopen history and exact source snapshots survive archive restore; reads reapply current private-source visibility. A reviewer without access to every source sees one opaque restricted-review blocker, with no source title, count or detail, and cannot close the matter (403); authorized counsel must review it. MATTER-004 workflow runs and document requests are checked live and each live run needs an explicit reopening decision; AGENT-007 and CLIENT-008 inherit live promise closure checks and explicit reopening decisions before their capabilities ship. REPORT-001 adds a required explicit legal outcome on closure, recorded only by the principal or responsible lawyer and retained across reopening. **Acceptance evidence:** Attempt closure with a trust balance and open court task, resolve or authorize exceptions, close and reopen while retaining the entire history.

**MATTER-008 — Number matters by firm scheme.** The principal configures the firm’s matter-number pattern from a starting number, padding, year, client number, practice-area code and separators, with optional per-client sequences. Each new matter receives the next unique number atomically, even when two open at once: two separately reviewed openings that involve only existing, unchanged parties both succeed concurrently, while any party insert, update or delete invalidates an older conflict review (SAT-002); a pattern change applies only to later matters, and imported matters keep their source numbers (MOVE-002) without colliding with new ones. Matter numbers appear on invoices, documents, calendar entries and search. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure a year, client number and four-digit sequence pattern starting at 1050, open two separately reviewed matters with only existing, unchanged parties concurrently and receive consecutive distinct numbers, then change a party and see an older review refused; import a Clio matter numbered 2019-0042 and confirm the next new matter does not collide; change the pattern and verify existing numbers are unchanged on the matter, its invoice and its documents.

**MATTER-009 — Search the whole firm from one box.** One search box finds matters by name, matter number or case number, contacts and aliases, notes, tasks, events, documents, email, invoices and payments the person may see, grouped by type with keyboard navigation and a phone layout. Results apply matter access, custom roles and ethical walls before any title, count or snippet is returned and link to the record; DOC-003 supplies document and email full text. **Acceptance evidence:** Search a client surname and find its matter, contact, note, task and invoice in grouped results; search a matter number and a case number; run the same queries as a walled-out principal and an unassigned assistant and receive no walled or unassigned record, title, count or snippet.

**DOC-001 — Store real working files.** Upload resumable large PDFs, DOCX, images, audio/video and bulk folders with per-file limits shown before transfer, quotas, malware quarantine and hash-verified originals. A 500 MiB scanned record and a multi-gigabyte matter set are ordinary supported work, not export-only attachments. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload a 500 MiB record, interrupt and resume, then bulk-upload a matter folder; download matching hashes and refuse access during quarantine. INTAKE-001’s R2 inquiry originals inherit DOC-001’s future resumable-upload and quarantine obligations before those doors ship.

**DOC-002 — Preview and compare versions.** Staff preview PDFs, images and office documents, annotate separately from originals and compare versions with author/time provenance. Concurrent saves create explicit conflicts; source citations continue to identify the reviewed version. **Acceptance evidence:** Open a PDF preview, annotate it, save conflicting Word edits and compare versions while downloading the unchanged original. Annotations are separate, version-bound page/section notes with author/time provenance; saving a note changes no original, current version or source citation. Appending an original requires its base document revision. A stale or racing save retains its exact attempted original as an explicit conflict beside the current version; an authorized resolution appends it as a new version (or identifies the already-retained identical version), retaining prior versions and citations. Office content previews identify their limitations and do not claim original layout, drawings, macro execution or recalculated formulas. Preview rendering remains in browser memory. Separate annotations and retained conflict originals follow the document’s access, archive, hold, erasure and restore-fence obligations, with each removed kind counted at disposal. DOC-005 and DOC-014 inherit these version, conflict and citation obligations before adding their save doors.

**DOC-003 — Search OCR and full text.** OCR scanned records and index permitted document text, metadata and email with matter/date/type filters, exact page snippets and index freshness. Search applies matter walls before snippets and includes deletion of all derivatives on disposal. **Acceptance evidence:** Find a phrase only present in a scanned page, open its citation, revoke access and confirm snippets and cached results disappear.

**DOC-004 — Organize and act on document sets.** Folders, tags, document types, saved views, bulk filing and duplicate detection support everyday matter navigation. Bulk operations preview their destinations and permissions and retain original identity and version history. Saved filters belong to the person within the matter, grant no sharing access and recheck current document access on every use. Metadata filing uses the existing uploader-or-principal edit authority and never changes readers. Folder, facet, saved-view and duplicate counts are computed only from accessible originals; duplicates are SHA-256 matches across retained versions of distinct documents, each original retained separately. Applying a recorded preview requires the same person and role, current matter/document access and unchanged document revisions; a preview applies once. **Acceptance evidence:** File a mixed production into two matter folders, catch a duplicate and bulk-retag it without exposing private files or replacing originals. Open the matter document folders and compare each displayed file count with its accessible contents before and after filing; private files contribute neither a name nor a count for an unauthorized reader.

**DOC-005 — Work in Microsoft Word.** Open matter DOCX files in Word through Microsoft 365, preserve tracked changes, comments and original versions, and save a new version back to the correct matter with conflict detection and access revocation. **Acceptance evidence:** Open a matter brief in Word, edit tracked changes, save back, race another save and inspect a visible conflict and both retained versions.

**DOC-006 — Assemble legal documents and forms.** Versioned Word/PDF templates merge typed matter fields, conditional clauses and repeating parties from approved questionnaires. Staff preview unresolved fields, maintain court-form versions and approve the generated DOCX/PDF before sending. Staff maintain immutable numbered templates with jurisdiction and court-form version labels, typed questionnaire fields (text, number, date, exact USD money, choice and yes/no), ordered paragraphs, answer-conditioned paragraphs and repeating matter parties. Merge fields use the matter’s adopted MATTER-001 version and canonical values, never the newest unadopted type; money renders in dollars with two decimals. Every saved questionnaire revision freezes its template version, answers, matter fields and party list and shows missing required or referenced values. Counsel approval covers that exact questionnaire and the generated DOCX/PDF whose hashes match the staff review downloads; incomplete, stale or unapproved final delivery is refused. Changed answers create a new comparable revision without rewriting earlier approvals or files. Approved files enter SAT-007 originals and inherit FIRM-006 retention/holds/erasure and BASE-001 archive recovery. Downloads are files for staff delivery, never a claim that Satchel sent them; CLIENT-006 and DOC-007 inherit exact-version approval before any sending or signing door ships. Jurisdiction and court-form version labels are firm-maintained, never a claim of court certification. **Acceptance evidence:** Assemble a two-party engagement and a jurisdiction form, change one questionnaire answer, compare revisions and refuse delivery with an unresolved required field.

**DOC-007 — Sign and file matter documents.** DocuSign and Inkwell connectors request ordered or parallel signatures on an approved exact version, remind permitted recipients and retain signed bytes, certificate, provider ID and failure/decline history. Revoking a request never overwrites a signed original. **Acceptance evidence:** Send a settlement release, decline then resend a revised version, complete it and replay the callback; inspect one signed version per completed request.

**DOC-008 — File Outlook email and attachments.** Microsoft 365/Outlook users file individual messages or approved threads and attachments to matters, retain sender/recipient headers and original .eml, associate sent replies and prevent duplicate filing across staff. Filing never grants a new matter reader. Approved matter-filing rules automatically capture matching incoming and sent messages; unmatched mail waits for staff assignment. **Acceptance evidence:** File an Outlook thread with an attachment, reply from Outlook, replay sync and inspect one linked message per provider ID with correct matter permissions. Approve an Outlook matter-filing rule, receive a matching email and attachment without manually filing them, and see them arrive in the correct matter once; an unmatched message waits for assignment, and replies composed in Outlook retain the same thread and source identities.

**DOC-009 — File Gmail email and attachments.** Google Workspace/Gmail users select matter labels or messages for filing, preserve original headers, threads and attachments, associate outbound replies and handle deleted or revoked mail access without losing filed evidence. Approved label-to-matter rules automatically capture matching mail and attachments while Gmail remains the composing and reply interface. **Acceptance evidence:** File a labeled Gmail conversation, add a reply, disconnect its grant and verify retained originals and a visible stopped-sync state. Enable a consented Gmail label-to-matter rule, receive a matching email and attachment without manually filing them, and inspect one automatic filing; compose and send the reply in Gmail and find it on the same matter thread without duplicate originals.

**DOC-010 — Connect SharePoint OneDrive and Drive.** Microsoft SharePoint/OneDrive and Google Drive connectors map selected folders and file versions to matters, track remote IDs and permission drift and offer controlled copy or linked-file custody. A revoked remote link is reported, never presented as a retained original. **Acceptance evidence:** Map folders from each service, update and revoke a remote file, and inspect the new version, failed access and explicit copy-versus-link custody.

**DOC-011 — Connect Box and Dropbox.** Firms map existing Box and Dropbox folders to matters with least-privilege grants, version references, sync diagnostics and permission reconciliation; neither service becomes an alternative firm access boundary. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect each provider, map one restricted folder, change remote permissions and confirm unauthorized clients and staff cannot acquire its contents.

**DOC-012 — Build medical and bill chronologies.** Authorized teams organize received medical records and bills by provider, date, treatment, charge and source page, identify gaps and duplicates, and reconcile totals without silently deciding causation or altering source evidence. Health-data access, agreements and processor configuration are explicit setup work. **Acceptance evidence:** Import a treatment packet and overlapping bill, review the source-linked chronology and discrepancy totals, and prevent publication before counsel approves it.

**DOC-013 — Prepare controlled evidence productions.** Counsel selects matter documents, privilege labels, redactions and Bates numbering; productions retain a manifest, privilege log, recipient and delivery proof while preserving unredacted originals and permitting recall of still-unopened shares. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a redacted production, review its privilege log, deliver to approved opposing counsel and inspect exact delivered bytes and the original retained separately.

**DOC-014 — Open matter folders on the desktop.** Staff install Satchel’s desktop drive for macOS and Windows, which shows only the matters they may access as folders in Finder or File Explorer, streams files on demand with optional per-matter offline pinning and opens them in any desktop application. Saving a file back records a new SAT-007 version with the saver’s identity and conflict detection, a file added to a matter folder is filed to that matter, and nothing is overwritten or deleted outside the matter’s retention and hold rules (FIRM-006). Ethical walls (FIRM-003), access removal and member deactivation take effect at the next sync and remove cached copies from the device; every open, save and offline pin is audited under FIRM-005. **Acceptance evidence:** On macOS and on Windows open an assigned matter folder in Finder and in File Explorer, edit a PDF in a desktop application and see a new retained version; race a web upload of the same file and inspect a visible conflict with both versions kept; drop a new file into the folder and find it filed to the matter; confirm a walled matter never appears; remove the user’s matter access and deactivate them and verify the folder and cached files disappear at the next sync and the audit shows each action.

**CAL-001 — Schedule matter appointments.** Matter calendars support appointments, recurring events, attendees, locations/video links, timezones, shared availability and cancellation history alongside distinct legal deadlines. Moving an appointment never moves an unrelated court deadline. Appointments are booked by the principal, lawyers and assistants who can see the matter. Attendees are active staff who can already see the matter; an invitation grants no access. A series repeats daily or weekly, every 1–12 days or weeks, for 2–104 occurrences at the same local wall-clock time in its IANA timezone, so its UTC instant shifts across daylight saving; a series with any occurrence at a local time that does not exist is refused, and an ambiguous local time uses the earlier instant. Canceling or moving one occurrence appends a reasoned, attributed change and never deletes the occurrence; a canceled occurrence stays canceled. The firm view lists the appointments and deadlines of every matter the viewer may see whose local dates fall in an inclusive range of at most 400 days, each read in its own timezone. Shared availability is free/busy: active staff see a colleague’s busy start and end times, with title and matter only for matters the viewer may see. CAL-002 and CAL-003 (calendar sync), CAL-011 (appointment reminders) and MOBILE-001/MOBILE-002 inherit these appointment, attendee and availability rules before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Book a recurring conference across daylight saving, invite two staff, cancel one instance and compare matter and firm views.

**CAL-002 — Synchronize Google Calendar both ways.** Selected Google calendars exchange event creation, edits, cancellations, attendees and recurrence with stable IDs, loop prevention, conflict resolution and visible token/failure state; matter confidentiality controls event detail. **Acceptance evidence:** Create an event in each system, edit concurrently, cancel a recurring instance and reconnect; inspect one consistent series with conflicts shown.

**CAL-003 — Synchronize Outlook calendars both ways.** Microsoft 365/Outlook calendars support the same two-way lifecycle, delegated calendars and attendee changes, with subscription renewal, missed-change recovery and explicit choice of which details leave the matter. **Acceptance evidence:** Edit a delegated Outlook appointment while Satchel is disconnected, reconnect and reconcile its updated attendees and cancellation without duplicate invitations.

**CAL-004 — Calculate LawToolBox deadlines.** Through a contracted LawToolBox integration, counsel chooses court, jurisdiction, trigger and service method, reviews computed dates and rule citations, and confirms publication to dependent tasks and calendars. Coverage and provider rule versions are visible. **Acceptance evidence:** Use a covered court and service trigger in a provider sandbox, review holiday-adjusted dates, refuse an unsupported court and publish only after attorney confirmation. Enter a replacement trial date once and inspect every LawToolBox-dependent deadline, its previous and proposed dates and rule/source references; after counsel confirms, each accepted deadline and connected calendar reflects that one trigger change.

**CAL-005 — Calculate CalendarRules deadlines.** CalendarRules is a supported alternative rules connector with court coverage, trigger/service inputs, rule versions, calculation provenance and attorney confirmation. Switching providers compares proposed dates rather than silently replacing confirmed deadlines. **Acceptance evidence:** Calculate one covered court schedule, compare it with an existing schedule and confirm differences before calendar changes; unsupported coverage leaves explicit manual review. Repeat the single trial-date change through CalendarRules and compare every dependent deadline with the provider’s schedule; keep unsupported or uncertain dates visibly unresolved for counsel rather than omitting them.

**CAL-006 — Propagate reviewed source changes.** A changed court order, service date or rules version presents affected dates and dependent tasks with old/new source passages. Counsel accepts or rejects each legal change; approved calendars and assignees then reconcile and acknowledge it. **Acceptance evidence:** Replace an order, inspect impacted deadlines, refuse automatic legal adoption, approve one change and verify all connected calendar copies and acknowledgment states. Change a trial date once, list every affected deadline and task, and reconcile accepted replacements to Google and Outlook without retaining an active superseded date or duplicating an event; CLIENT-008 supplies the separately reviewed portal/email client notice.

**CAL-007 — Remind and escalate deadlines.** Rules define advance reminders, channels, quiet hours and escalation to a backup lawyer; acknowledgment differs from completion, and completion needs evidence of the underlying act. Missed or uncertain delivery stays visible until resolved. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule a deadline reminder, fail one delivery, restart before escalation and complete the deadline with a filing receipt; only that receipt closes the obligation. Set a seven-day reminder to the assigned lawyer, advance through its due instant and inspect the actual recipient, delivery result and one escalation after failed delivery; reassignment before sending must prevent delivery to the former owner.

**CAL-008 — Show firm deadline coverage.** Lawyers see firm and matter agenda, upcoming limitation dates, conflicts, unconfirmed dates and absence coverage. Reports identify each source, owner, confirmation status and next action; an extracted date never appears as confirmed. Deadlines carry a kind (deadline, limitation, hearing or filing) and a responsible owner, set by the principal or a lawyer from active staff who already see the matter, with append-only owner history. The agenda lists, for the matters the viewer may see, every non-superseded deadline and every uncanceled CAL-001 appointment occurrence in an inclusive local-date range of at most 400 days; upcoming limitation dates are every proposed or confirmed limitation from the range start onward. A conflict is two appointment occurrences that overlap in time and share an organizer or attendee, reported only among items the viewer may see. The principal records anyone’s absence and staff record their own; all active staff see who is out, when, and who covers, while the reason is visible only to the principal and the absent person. The principal or the absent person assigns coverage to another active staff member; coverage grants no matter access. Next action follows this precedence: unconfirmed date, no owner, owner absent without coverage, coverer cannot see the matter, time conflict, then prepare and complete (or attend). A proposed date, including one an agent extracted and a person accepted as a proposal, always shows as unconfirmed until a lawyer confirms it. The CSV export carries date, time, timezone, kind, matter, title, source, owner, confirmation, coverage, conflicts and next action, and is recorded in the action audit. CAL-002/003 (synced calendars), CAL-004/005 (rule-computed dates), CAL-006 and MATTER-003/006 (tasks and handoffs) inherit these agenda, owner and coverage obligations before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** View overlapping hearings and an unconfirmed limitations date, assign coverage and export the agenda with source and confirmation columns.
