**CAL-009 — File and serve through InfoTrack.** An authorized lawyer approves exact filing documents, court, service recipients and fees; InfoTrack submits through covered networks and returns acceptance/rejection, stamped copies, service proof and costs to the matter. Submission alone is never filing completion. **Acceptance evidence:** Approve a sandbox filing, receive rejection, correct and resubmit with a new revision, then reconcile stamped acceptance, service proof and expense without duplicate charges. Submit a fourteen-exhibit filing and inspect each exhibit’s manifest entry and stamped acceptance; the matter’s filed-exhibit count reaches fourteen only after all fourteen are accepted, and a rejected exhibit remains open.

**CAL-010 — Track court docket changes.** Connect PACER through an authorized docket provider such as CourtListener RECAP where available and court/provider accounts for coverage, attach returned docket entries and orders, and propose related work with a lawyer reviewing legal effects and provider fees. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive an amended order twice, inspect one docket entry and source artifact, and require counsel review before changing a legal deadline.

**CAL-011 — Remind staff of appointments and tasks.** Each staff member receives in-app and email reminders, and push reminders under MOBILE-002, for their appointments and tasks at firm-default or per-item offsets, with snooze and dismiss. Reminders follow reassignment, cancellation and rescheduling, fire once across restarts and carry no confidential detail outside the authenticated app. A person who relies on Google or Outlook reminders for synced events can choose calendar-only reminders, so the same event never reminds twice. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a task due tomorrow with a one-hour reminder and an appointment with a 15-minute reminder; reassign the task, reschedule the appointment and restart the worker; verify the new owner alone receives one task reminder, the appointment reminder fires once at the new time and the email carries only a link and a minimal subject; set calendar-only for a synced event and verify Satchel sends no reminder for it.

**CLIENT-001 — Invite a secure client portal.** A client or authorized co-client signs in to only expressly shared matters, with separate payer access and revocable delegates. Staff preview the client view; internal notes, other clients and privileged drafts never leak through search or notifications. **Acceptance evidence:** Invite two co-clients and a payer, share one release, revoke a delegate and exercise direct portal file and message URLs for each identity.

**CLIENT-002 — Retain secure two-way messages.** Portal conversations retain matter, participants, attachments, delivery/read states and staff assignments. Recipients receive minimal notifications and open confidential content inside the authenticated portal. **Acceptance evidence:** Send a confidential attachment, receive a client reply, inspect the retained thread and unread queue and verify email notifications contain no confidential body.

**CLIENT-003 — Chase document requests to receipt.** Staff request specific records with instructions, owner, due date and acceptance criteria. Clients upload securely, staff accept or explain deficiencies, and authorized reminders continue only until accepted, stopped or escalated. **Acceptance evidence:** Request two records, receive an incomplete upload, send a permitted clarification and close only the accepted item while the second remains due.

**CLIENT-004 — Give clients tasks and events.** The portal shows shared upcoming events, client tasks, due dates, completion instructions and acknowledgments; clients cannot mark a lawyer’s legal deadline complete or change confirmed court dates. **Acceptance evidence:** Share a preparation task and hearing, complete the client task from a phone and refuse a client attempt to alter the hearing deadline.

**CLIENT-005 — Text clients and leads with Twilio.** Two-way SMS/MMS through the firm’s registered Twilio number retains conversations on the correct lead/matter, consent, delivery/failure and opt-outs. A guided setup walks the principal through connecting or creating the Twilio account, buying or porting a number, US A2P 10DLC brand and campaign registration prefilled from firm settings, approval tracking and a test message; texting stays disabled with a visible reason until registration is approved. Quiet hours and recipient confirmation are part of setup; sensitive content uses portal links. Reviewed reminders can request an event confirmation reply such as C; matching replies record one acknowledgment on that event, never legal completion. Before this capability ships, enforce its own recorded sending or sync authority and INTAKE-004’s merged-identity consent obligations; a contact merge supplies neither authority nor consent. **Acceptance evidence:** Complete the guided setup through sandbox registration states and see texting stay disabled while the campaign is pending; after approval text a consenting lead, file a reply, process STOP and verify pending reminders halt without exposing private message content. Send a consented mediation reminder asking the client to reply C to confirm; receive C twice and inspect one event acknowledgment on the correct matter, without completing a legal deadline or sending a second confirmation.

**CLIENT-006 — Deliver and reconcile email.** Connected Microsoft/Gmail or the firm’s configured transactional mail provider sends reviewed client correspondence and invoice notifications, retains provider references and bounce/complaint states and avoids blindly resending an uncertain delivery. Before this capability ships, enforce its own recorded sending or sync authority and INTAKE-004’s merged-identity consent obligations; a contact merge supplies neither authority nor consent. **Acceptance evidence:** Send a reviewed letter, simulate a bounce and lost acknowledgment at the provider edge, and inspect one attempt with a visible next human action.

**CLIENT-007 — Keep call records and authorized recordings.** Staff log calls, participants, advice notes and follow-ups and link recordings/transcripts obtained through a consented phone provider. Recording permission and US state consent policy are checked before recording; staff approve transcript-derived work. **Acceptance evidence:** Log a call and task, connect a consented recording and refuse capture without the required consent, then inspect permissioned transcript access.

**CLIENT-008 — Send reviewed matter updates.** Matter events produce draft client updates with source links and outstanding client actions. Counsel reviews wording, recipients and promises; approved scheduled updates track delivery and unresolved replies through completion. Before shipping, its reviewed promises participate in MATTER-007’s live closure inventory, remaining unresolved until evidenced fulfillment or an individual counsel carry decision; reopening restores only explicitly approved workflows and existing access. **Acceptance evidence:** Generate an update after an order, remove privileged strategy, approve its delivery and receive a reply that reopens the responsible person’s follow-up queue. Move a confirmed trial date, review the old/new date and cited order in the draft update, then deliver the approved update to the authenticated portal and through CLIENT-006 email; verify both delivery states and that an unapproved change notifies nobody.

**CLIENT-009 — Control sharing and communication preferences.** Record communication channels, language, accessibility needs, legal-representative authority and recipient verification; revoking consent or portal access stops new automated contact and invalidates outstanding links where possible while preserving historic delivered records. **Acceptance evidence:** Change a client’s representative and SMS preference mid-sequence, then verify future recipients, link access and the retained old delivery history.

**CLIENT-010 — Automated client reminders.** per-matter opt-in by the responsible counsel, template approved once by counsel, scheduled invoice and appointment reminders under a rate cap, withdrawal of consent stops the next send, each send audited with the template version.

**TIME-001 — Run timers and timesheets.** Timekeepers start, pause, resume and switch matter timers, enter work on weekly timesheets, distinguish billable/nonbillable activity and submit reviewed time without overlapping unnoticed timers. A timekeeper also reviews and posts a complete drafted day with editable durations and UTBMS codes; posting is idempotent and shows exact daily hours and USD totals. Every staff member keeps only their own timers and timesheet, on matters they see. Timers live on the server, so one started on a phone resumes on a desktop. A person has at most one running timer: starting or resuming another pauses the running one in the same step and says so, so timers never overlap unnoticed. Each closed timer interval (pause, stop or switch) drafts exactly one entry attributed to its timekeeper: elapsed time rounded up to a whole minute (at most 1,440, longer intervals labeled for review), dated by the interval start in the firm timezone (UTC before firm setup), at the rate TIME-003 resolves for its work date (the firm default rate and increment when no agreement rule matches). The weekly timesheet runs Monday to Sunday; timekeepers add drafts and edit duration (1–1,440 minutes), billability and UTBMS task (letter plus three digits, e.g. L110) and activity (A plus three digits) codes, checked for format only until TIME-007 supplies firm code sets, or reject a draft. Post day or Submit week turns each remaining draft into one immutable entry, refused while the timekeeper has a running timer; rejected drafts are excluded, posted drafts are final and a repeated post records nothing. Daily and weekly totals show exact hours and minutes of non-rejected drafts and billable USD at TIME-003’s price (billed minutes, rounded up to the agreed increment, × hourly cents / 60, less any agreed discount, half-up to whole cents). Nonbillable entries are recorded but refused on bills. TIME-002 suggestions, TIME-003 rate schedules and TIME-007 code sets inherit these drafts and the posting rule before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Start a timer on phone, resume on desktop, switch matters and submit the week; inspect one attributed entry per approved interval. Review a day of draft entries, edit durations and UTBMS codes, then Post day; inspect one attributed posted entry per accepted draft and exact daily hours/USD totals, with rejected drafts excluded and a repeated post producing no duplicate work.

**TIME-002 — Capture email calendar and document activity.** With explicit staff permission, Microsoft Word/Outlook and Google email/calendar/document activity becomes private time suggestions linked to matter sources. Staff review duration and billability, merge overlaps and exclude personal content before anything is billed. **Acceptance evidence:** Work on an email, meeting and Word draft, review suggestions, discard personal activity and accept nonoverlapping time once despite repeated sync. Inspect the draft day assembled from the email, calendar and document sources, open each source reference, edit an inaccurate suggestion and pass only the reviewed suggestions to TIME-001 day posting.

**TIME-003 — Apply versioned rates and budgets.** Fee agreements support attorney, matter, client, task and effective-date rates, rounding increments, discounts, nonbillable work and budgets with alerts. Old work retains its agreed rate; changing a rate never rewrites an issued bill. Agreement rules are append-only versions at firm, client (the matter’s recorded client name, exact match) or matter scope, optionally naming a timekeeper and a UTBMS task, each with an hourly USD-cents rate, a 1–60-minute rounding increment, a discount in basis points and a billable flag, effective from an inclusive date compared with the work date; a second rule with the same scope, timekeeper, task and date is refused. Precedence: a matter rule beats the client’s, which beats the firm’s; within one, a rule naming the timekeeper beats one that does not, then one naming the task, then the latest effective date on or before the work date; with no matching rule the FIRM-001 default rate and increment apply with no discount. Billed minutes are worked minutes rounded up to the increment; the charge is billed minutes × hourly cents × (10,000 − discount basis points) / 600,000, half-up to whole cents. A nonbillable rule makes matching work nonbillable (recorded, never billed). Timesheet drafts are priced from the agreement on their work date and posting freezes that price on the immutable entry, as does recording an entry without a rate; an explicit hourly rate on an entry or draft is recorded exactly as entered (SAT-004), with no increment or discount. Recorded entries keep their price when rules change, and issued bills keep their snapshot and exported bytes. Until FIRM-002 adds billing staff, the principal sets firm and client rules, and the principal or a lawyer who sees the matter sets matter rules and budgets. A matter budget is a versioned USD-cents amount with an alert percent; used is the recorded cents of every billable entry on the matter (time and disbursements). Each level alerts once per budget version, in the same step as the recording or budget change that crosses it: threshold when used × 100 ≥ budget × percent, exceeded when used > budget. Alerts are shown on the matter in Satchel and audited; no email is sent. TIME-002 suggestions, TIME-007 code sets and every later time-recording door or time import inherit this pricing and the budget check before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Set a client override and future rate change, record work either side, cross the matter budget and inspect correct charges and the alert.

**TIME-004 — Bill flat and recurring fees.** Flat-fee milestones, recurring retainers, capped fees and blended arrangements record earned timing, included work and approved exceptions. Recurring schedules produce reviewable draft bills without silently recognizing unearned trust funds as revenue. The principal or a lawyer who sees the matter records immutable, explicitly reviewed fee terms: arrangement, USD cents, included work, permitted exceptions (or none), agreement reference, earning event and whether earned fees may be drawn from trust. Unknown earning or draw-down eligibility is refused with its reason. Flat, milestone and retainer arrangements create one nonhourly fee per due occurrence; once uses the reviewed start date, and monthly uses the first day of each calendar month from the reviewed start month through the inclusive final month. The first monthly date must be a month boundary. The scheduled Worker uses the firm IANA timezone and each plan reviewer's current authority and matter access, processing plans separately so a blocked plan cannot stop another plan on the same matter; counsel can also run the due schedule through a date. A unique plan/period identity survives restart and restore, including a voided occurrence, so replay never prepares another bill for it. Plans do not alter earlier drafts or invoices. Due processing only prepares drafts, earns zero, sends nothing and transfers nothing; failures remain visible with the missing guideline or other reason. Before approving a fee bill or its additive correction, counsel explicitly confirms the reviewed earning event and records source evidence; milestone earning also requires explicit completion, a future period cannot earn, and period-end earning is allowed only after the complete monthly period (or the once plan's end date) has passed in the firm timezone. Approval records the exact earned USD cents separately from trust custody. Prohibited draw-down is refused even for an earned bill; permitted draw-down still requires the existing same-matter, cleared-funds, officer and bank-result workflow, never inferred allocation or automatic movement. Capped and blended plans apply to selected recorded work within their inclusive date range, cannot overlap another capped/blended plan on the matter, and must be selected at preparation whenever selected time intersects that range. Caps cover time fees across all live drafts, approved invoices and additive corrections under that plan, with no monthly reset: chronological lines consume the remaining cap and can become zero; disbursements retain their exact amounts. Blended time uses worked whole minutes times the reviewed single hourly USD-cent rate divided by 60, rounded half-up to cents, independent of the original recorded hourly rate or increment. A permitted exception needs a separate counsel reference at preparation and uses the recorded entry amounts; no-exception plans refuse it. Positive corrections cannot exceed a reviewed cap or raise a flat, milestone, retainer or blended source above its originally reviewed line amount; a courtesy reduction can be restored only up to that amount. Source reservations and revision checks continue to prevent duplicate billing, and originals and terms remain immutable through corrections and archive recovery. Under a client LEDES guideline, nonhourly fees are F fee lines, one unit at the exact fee with the reviewed task/activity and timekeeper identity, never expenses or fabricated hours; all active-code, narrative and client guideline checks apply, XML 2.1.3 uses flat charge type F, and approval freezes both exports. TIME-005, TIME-008, BILL-001, BILL-004 and BILL-016 inherit these earning, cap, eligibility, source and nonhourly-code obligations before their new fee or bill doors ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a monthly flat fee and a milestone fee, run the due schedule twice and inspect one draft per period with separate earned and trust balances.

**TIME-005 — Manage contingency and settlements.** Record versioned contingency percentages, tiered outcomes, expenses, liens, medical providers and referral allocations. A settlement statement explains gross recovery, costs, fees and each disbursement; counsel and authorized finance staff approve before money movement. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a settlement with a lien reduction and expense recovery, compare all allocations to gross funds and refuse disbursement until approvals and cleared funds exist.

CT policy ruling, 27 October 2026: APPROVE WITH RIDERS; TIME-005 remains PARTIAL. Native human counsel reviews the exact versioned contingency agreement, selected outcome, percentage basis, earning condition and completed earning evidence. Percentages use basis points and half-up USD-cent rounding. Referral allocations divide the counsel fee and never add a separate client charge; the restricted statement retains original obligations, reductions, source evidence and an exact reconciliation to gross recovery. Different counsel and designated trust-officer people approve each current exact statement by default. For a sole-practitioner firm, the native principal may explicitly enable a recorded separation waiver identifying its reason, scope, actor, effective version and time.

Under that setting one currently authorized person may hold both capabilities but must record two distinct capacity approvals against the same revision. A replacement statement requires fresh approvals. The setting establishes product authority only and does not establish that a legal requirement is waivable. Current roles, officer designation, matter grants, ethical walls and cleared unreserved same-matter funds are rechecked at every applicable final action. Readiness neither reserves funds nor authorizes spending, recognizes revenue, issues an invoice or moves money. TIME-004 earning and eligibility controls and TIME-007 coding and guideline controls remain required before settlement fees enter billing. General audit retains attributable decision and revision metadata; settlement amounts and source documents remain restricted evidence. Archives retain history without restoring sessions or execution authority. CT remaining-proof inventory, preserved from the 27 October ruling: Remaining TIME-005 proof: preserve and complete the original settlement-to-disbursement acceptance; prove fractional-cent fee and referral rounding, reserved-fund exclusion, changed approver roles, officer designation and ethical walls, the recorded sole-practitioner setting, complete attributable audit, settlement-specific retention and erasure, restored-authority refusal and settlement-fee earning and coding integration. Bind the exact approved statement and each allocation into disbursement preparation and final approval, with current funds and authority rechecked. Record the clause’s own populated and refused screens at 1440 and 390 on the landed SHA; each UI acceptance test need assert its points at only one width. Native implementation evidence: `tests/satchel/fee-plans.test.mjs` — “Settlement statements reconcile recovery and refuse spending without current approvals and cleared funds” invokes settlementExecutionFlow in `tests/satchel/settlement-execution-flow.mjs` (fractional-cent fee and referral rounding, reserved-fund exclusion, exact payee and amount binding, changed roles, officer designation, grants, custom ceilings and walls, recorded sole-practitioner approval, attributed restricted audit and restored-authority refusal), settlementBillingFlow in `tests/satchel/settlement-billing-flow.mjs` (explicit earning and eligibility, active codes and guideline checks, immutable nonhourly LEDES, exact source and once-only charging, current authority at transfer approval and bank reconciliation, reciprocal double-spend refusal), and settlementRetentionFlow in `tests/satchel/settlement-retention-flow.mjs` (legal holds, principal-only expired disposal, preserved attribution, irreversible restricted-payload erasure and the older-archive fence). `tests/satchel/fee-plans-journey.test.mjs` — “Settlement workspace prepares recovery, records sole-practitioner settings and binds exact disbursements with approval and funds refusals at 1440 and 390” invokes settlementExecutionJourney in `tests/satchel/settlement-browser.mjs` through populated and refused settlement and firm-setting screens. Execution semantics: every trust disbursement on a settlement matter binds its current exact statement, allocation index, payee and amount; counsel and finance approvals are rechecked at preparation and final ledger posting. Full gross recovery must be covered by current cleared availability plus this statement’s own reserved or posted allocations; unrelated reservations remain excluded. Pending allocations must be declined before replacement, and a posted allocation keeps its original statement. A billed counsel fee and its generic counsel or referral disbursements cannot consume the same recovery twice. Settings changes require fresh capacity approvals. Archives retain policy and approval history, but a fresh installation stamp prevents restored history from supplying execution authority; restored settings require a new principal decision. Restricted text disposal follows the current expired matter retention schedule, refuses active holds and preserves identities and approval attribution; a retained settlement fee bill keeps its original source evidence and refuses disposal. Bank activity is recorded and reconciled through the existing trust doors; no provider execution or legal compliance is claimed. Fresh-judgment assertion map: `tests/satchel/fee-plans.test.mjs` — “Settlement statements reconcile recovery and refuse spending without current approvals and cleared funds”, lines 185–189 asserts all original obligations, reductions, net amounts and source references; lines 201–213 refuses pending replacement without changing terms, approvals or custody and permits replacement after decline; lines 215–226 asserts both attributable terms-review records and their archive preservation. `docs/evidence/time005-assertions.md` records the three formerly surviving mutations and their failing assertions. Native assertions are supplied for fresh ct judgment; no completion is counted.

**TIME-006 — Capture reimbursable expenses.** Staff attach receipts and vendor/provider references, distinguish firm overhead, client disbursements and advanced costs, apply approved markup/tax treatment and reconcile a repeated filing-provider charge to one billable expense. Native detailed expenses record vendor, vendor reference, accounting code, overhead/client-disbursement/advanced-cost classification and an exact original receipt version. Overhead is nonbillable. The exact trimmed source-system/charge-reference pair identifies a reported charge across the firm: an unchanged replay returns its existing entry, changed details refuse, and concurrent submissions commit at most one entry. References are imported assertions, not provider verification; no markup is inferred. Existing document access and erasure rules apply to receipt links. Expense provenance is frozen into reviewed bill lines and CSV and survives restart and archive restore. **Acceptance evidence:** Import an InfoTrack fee and upload its receipt, replay the charge and inspect one approved disbursement with its source and accounting mapping.

**TIME-007 — Code LEDES and UTBMS work.** Firms configure UTBMS task/activity/expense codes and client guidelines; validate timekeeper IDs, narratives, rates and required fields; export LEDES 1998B and supported client-required LEDES XML with acceptance/rejection tracking. Until FIRM-002 adds billing staff, the principal configures the firm’s UTBMS code sets (task letter plus three digits, activity A plus three digits, expense E plus three digits; codes are retired, never deleted), each team member’s unique LEDES timekeeper ID and classification (PT, AS, OC, PL, LA or OT), and each client’s billing guideline. With no configured code of a kind, TIME-001’s format check is the whole rule; once a kind has codes, every entry, timesheet draft, bill coding and correction must use an active one. A guideline is an append-only version for the matter’s recorded client name (exact match, as TIME-003) naming the LEDES client ID and law-firm ID, whether task, activity and expense codes are required, a minimum narrative length, banned narrative phrases (case-insensitive), maximum hourly rates by classification and a required billing increment (0 for none); every fee line needs a timekeeper ID, and no LEDES field may contain | or []. A bill prepared for a client with a guideline is a LEDES bill: preparation checks every line against the current version and the firm code sets and refuses the whole bill naming each failing line and reason; codes may be chosen per line at preparation without changing the recorded entry. Before BILL-015 cutover, preparation reserves a unique invoice number (matter number, dash, the matter’s bill count including voided drafts; numbers are never reused) and approval freezes a LEDES 1998B file beside the reviewed CSV: YYYYMMDD dates, billing period from the earliest to the latest line date, units = billed hours to four decimals (half-up), unit cost = the hourly rate, and LINE_ITEM_ADJUSTMENT_AMOUNT carrying the agreed discount and rounding so the line total = units × unit cost (half-up to cents) + adjustment exactly; expenses are one unit at their amount. Downloading the frozen file marks the bill exported; bills for clients without a guideline stay plain reviewed bills. Counsel record the client’s e-billing outcome by importing its file (rows INVOICE_NUMBER|LINE_ITEM_NUMBER|STATUS|REASON, header optional, a blank line number meaning the whole invoice, a rejection needing its reason) only for that exported invoice; outcomes are append-only, labelled “imported from the e-billing file, not verified with the vendor” (Satchel never contacts the vendor), a re-imported file records nothing, and the invoice’s status follows its latest file (rejected if any row rejects). A rejected or wrong line is corrected through the existing reviewed correction branch: the correction may change the line’s codes, narrative or amount, is rechecked against the current guideline and code sets, and its LEDES file is a full replacement invoice numbered <original>-R<n> at every source’s current amount and coding, while Satchel’s ledger records only the additive delta, so no entry is charged twice and the original export is unchanged. BILL-001 batches, TIME-004/TIME-005 fee kinds, TIME-008 bulk entry and every later bill or time door inherit the code-set and guideline checks before they ship. The supported client-required XML profile is LEDES XML 2.1.3, validated in the public-door journeys against the unchanged [official LEDES Oversight Committee XSD](https://ledes.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/LEDES213xsd.zip) (`fixtures/ledes/Ledes213.xsd`; [format history](https://ledes.org/ledes-xml-ebilling-ver-2-1-format/)). The principal enables XML in an append-only guideline with explicit work country for invoice lines, firm vendor ID, the client-assigned firm vendor ID, client billing address/phone, firm billing-contact first/last name and email, and a client-assigned matter ID recorded separately for each matter; an expense-only invoice also names a configured billing timekeeper and its recorded hourly USD-cents rate for the required summary. Preparation checks the schema field lengths, XML characters, billed timekeeper names recorded as Last, First and IDs (at most 10 characters), and snapshots these details and the current US firm name/address/phone. Approval freezes a separate immutable XML artifact and digest; either download marks the bill exported and uses the same imported-outcome and reviewed-replacement flow. XML contains every fee and expense once, original line numbers as globally unique detail file-item numbers, USD, ISO dates, zero unrecorded tax and funds-applied amounts, exact matter/invoice totals, and the replacement reference in a standard extension. XML units are billed hours rounded half-up to two decimals as its XSD requires; base is the exact units × rate to four decimal dollar places, and a four-decimal signed line adjustment makes the exported line total equal the reviewed USD cents exactly (including discounts and rounding). XML does not claim vendor acceptance; settings changes and later replacements never rewrite either frozen export. Bills prepared without an XML profile retain their existing 1998B artifact; enabling the profile applies to future preparations and substantive reviewed corrections. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a coded insurer bill, reject a missing activity code, export valid LEDES 1998B and XSD-valid XML 2.1.3 and import a rejection to correct via a reviewed revision without duplicate charges.
BILL-015 cutover is the principal’s first saved scheme.

fragments.text: **TIME-008 — Submit bulk work and allocate revenue.** Authorized staff bulk-enter or import time/expenses with per-row validation and attribution, while firm-approved origination/responsible-attorney revenue allocations and commissions use collected revenue and reversible source links. **Acceptance evidence:** Import a weekly timesheet with one invalid row, repair it, bill and partially collect; inspect attributed collections and commission calculations without changing original timekeeper records. Bulk batches retain immutable originals, repaired inputs and normalized review snapshots. The principal may attribute work to eligible staff; other native timekeepers import their own work. Creator and original timekeeper remain separate, with current authority, original and current matter access, walls, pricing, codes, expense provenance and approved cost basis checked before atomic posting. Staff costs and compensation decisions remain principal-only. Allocation rules are explicit append-only principal approvals of the exact supporting document version and digest, agreement citation, origination and responsible-attorney shares, and commission basis points. Each allocation explicitly reviews an actual net operating collection and freezes its invoice components and rule version; receipt face value and unapplied credit are never substituted for invoice-applied cash. A cleared bank application retains its explicitly reviewed earned-work and tax split; only its earned-work component is apportioned across pre-tax source lines. Unsplit collected cents are apportioned across net invoice lines and tax by largest remainder with source-identity tie order. Only the fee portion is shared; expenses and tax remain distinct. Attorney shares and the firm remainder conserve every fee cent, and commissions round half-up from each share. Prior returns are excluded from the approved original; subsequent linked releases and reversals subtract successive calculations on that same frozen basis exactly once. Invoice value, unpaid balances, pending payments, trust custody and write-offs confer no commission. A bank-cleared operating application is distinct from its preceding trust custody. Rule changes never rewrite original work, cost snapshots, bills or earlier allocations. These are internal calculations and authorize no payout. `API.md` documents the public doors and exact semantics.

**BILL-001 — Run prebill review and batch invoices.** Billing staff prepare prebills by matter, payer, period and arrangement; lawyers review narratives, exclusions and write-downs; batch issue uses exact approvals, unique invoice numbers assigned under BILL-015 and immutable PDF and line artifacts with an audit trail. Each PDF is rendered from the matter’s assigned BILL-013 template, and the issued invoice records that exact template revision, so later template edits never change it. During approval billing staff may request that available client trust pay the invoice through TRUST-004; the invoice issues showing the trust application once the trust officer approves it. After issue an invoice changes only by a SAT-006 correction or a BILL-016 void and rebill. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare three matters in one run, return one prebill, approve two and issue twice; inspect two issued invoices, each naming its template revision and a BILL-015 number, and unchanged source reservations. Request trust application to one approved invoice and, after trust-officer approval, see it issue as paid from trust.
BILL-015 cutover is the principal’s first saved scheme.

fragments.text: **BILL-002 — Deliver invoices and payer statements.** Issue and deliver reviewed PDFs plus authenticated online payment links by portal/email with payer details, due dates, matter summaries and trust statements. Each PDF carries the firm’s logo, address and remittance details, the client and matter header, payment terms, a QR code and link to that invoice’s payment page and the trust balance as its BILL-013 template specifies. Track actual provider delivery/failure separately from export or queue success. Once an invoice is voided under BILL-016, its delivered payment link, portal page and QR code refuse payment and name the replacement invoice. **Acceptance evidence:** Issue an invoice to a client and insurer, inspect delivered artifacts for logo, remittance block, terms and trust balance, scan the QR code to reach only that invoice’s payment page, inspect one bounced notification, then resend only with recorded authorization.

**BILL-003 — Split payers and handle foreign invoices.** Fee agreements allocate fixed or percentage responsibility across clients, insurers and third parties with separate privacy and payment status. USD is the US default; explicitly configured foreign-currency invoices preserve original currency, approved FX rate and USD accounting differences. **Acceptance evidence:** Split a $1,000 bill between two payers, issue a foreign-currency bill under an approved agreement and reconcile payments without converting trust ledgers silently.

**BILL-004 — Calculate US billing tax explicitly.** The firm configures counsel/accountant-reviewed service and expense tax treatment by US jurisdiction, exemptions and rounding, optionally using Avalara for supported calculation. Tax lines preserve calculation inputs and provider result; unknown treatment blocks issuance for review. Native tax-reviewed additive corrections retain the original immutable reviewed rule, including exemptions, rates and per-line rounding. Each correction records the prior and corrected nonnegative source bases and their separately rounded tax; its signed tax delta is corrected tax minus prior tax, never a rounded percentage of the delta. A later rule cannot rewrite an earlier invoice or correction. Exact-revision calculation and counsel approval precede issue/export; original CSV/PDF bytes remain unchanged. A legacy correction without a reviewed original tax basis cannot invent one. Every draft approval, including an unconfigured legacy draft or an exemption, requires its exact-revision reviewed calculation. Trust requests require retained counsel-reviewed permitted tax draw-down and an explicit reference and nonnegative integer USD-cent allocations to earned base and tax; unknown or prohibited eligibility refuses. Each component is bounded separately after pending reservations, cleared payments and exact full reversals, while the total also respects cleared same-matter funds. Approval, bank submission and clearance recheck the retained eligibility and allocation; a pending legacy request cannot bypass them. Tax contributes to invoice due, never earned service revenue, and the existing officer, bank-evidence and reversal doors still apply. A client-reviewed immutable mapping must match the bill's recorded client and LEDES client ID and name the 1998B tax expense code, XML tax identity/type and review reference; missing, mismatched, invalid or retired mapping refuses approval. LEDES 1998B retains net source rows and appends mapped expense rows for nonzero per-source tax, with tax included in invoice totals. XML 2.1.3 uses standard fee/expense tax summaries and tax definitions, fractional rates, and a reviewed_tax extension carrying each exact source base and tax. Replacement LEDES exports contain the complete corrected invoice and the actual issued parent number; native CSV/PDF corrections retain only the signed additive difference. Original CSV/PDF/LEDES files and allocations survive restart and archive restore unchanged. No Avalara calculation or client/vendor verification is claimed. **Acceptance evidence:** Bill taxable and exempt lines to two US jurisdictions, inspect calculation provenance and refuse a bill with unreviewed treatment.

**BILL-005 — Collect through 8am LawPay.** Connect the firm’s contracted LawPay account for hosted card/eCheck payments, trust or operating destination, saved authorization, payment links, text-to-pay links sent through CLIENT-005 and QR payment links on invoices. Billing staff also take a card or eCheck payment a client authorizes by phone by keying it into LawPay’s hosted virtual-terminal fields inside Satchel, recording the client’s authorization and allocating it to the chosen invoice or trust request in the same step; card and account numbers never reach Satchel’s servers, logs or archives. Optional card surcharging applies only to operating payments by credit card, in US states the firm has enabled it for and within card-network caps, is disclosed before payment and is never added to debit cards or trust deposits. Show pending, cleared, failed and returned states; fees and chargebacks must not invade client trust principal. **Acceptance evidence:** Pay a sandbox operating invoice and a trust request, duplicate webhooks and return an eCheck; inspect exactly-once allocation, separated fees and visible reversal. Enable surcharging, pay an operating invoice by credit card from a text-to-pay link and see the disclosed surcharge as its own line; refuse a surcharge on a debit card and on a trust request, and pay a second invoice from its QR code. As billing staff key a sandbox card read out by phone into the hosted fields against an operating invoice, record the authorization and see the invoice paid in one step; confirm no card number appears in Satchel requests, logs or archive, and refuse the same action to an assistant without billing rights. As the client open an issued $3,250 invoice’s payment link and pay online by hosted card or bank/eCheck; inspect the invoice number, exact allocated amount and paid state only after the provider confirms payment, and prove a failed or uncertain attempt never marks it paid.

**BILL-006 — Collect through Stripe legal configurations.** Stripe is an alternative for firm-approved operating payments and any explicitly supported trust configuration, using hosted tokenization and account verification. Trust collection cannot be enabled until the firm verifies a compliant bank/processor arrangement that protects client principal from fees and chargebacks. **Acceptance evidence:** Collect a sandbox operating card/ACH payment and inspect reconciliation; attempt trust enablement without verified protection and refuse it, then test an approved trust arrangement. As the client pay an issued invoice online from its invoice page using hosted card and, on another invoice, ACH; replay provider events and verify the exact invoice allocation and visible pending/paid/returned states without duplicate collection.

**BILL-007 — Reconcile payments refunds and disputes.** Provider events reconcile invoices, receipts, settlement batches, processor fees, bank deposits, ACH returns, refunds and disputes with stable external IDs. Refunds and write-offs require finance approval and append-only corrections; unknown settlement never appears paid. **Acceptance evidence:** Lose a charge response, replay callbacks, settle a batch and approve a partial refund; reconcile invoice, processor, bank and ledger totals with no duplicate collection.

**BILL-008 — Run consented payment plans.** Authorized staff define installments, start date, balance allocation, payment method mandate and hardship changes. The scheduler charges only under current consent, prevents duplicate attempts and stops/escalates failed, disputed or revoked installments. A plan or saved-card autopay moved in from another system under MOVE-008 starts paused and charges nothing until the client re-authorizes it under LawPay or Stripe. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a three-installment plan, process one, revoke consent before the next due date and restart; inspect one charge and a stopped plan with a human task. Import a source plan and confirm it stays paused, charging nothing, until the client’s recorded re-authorization.

**BILL-009 — Pursue collections until resolved.** Aging queues, retainer replenishment and overdue invoices drive firm-approved reminder sequences with owner, next due date, attempt/reply states and contact limits. Disputes, promises to pay, hardship and representation changes route to people; confirmed payment, including an offline payment recorded through BILL-012 or a trust application approved through TRUST-004, stops future contact, a partial payment continues the sequence for the remainder only, and reversing that payment reopens the sequence. Voiding an invoice under BILL-016 ends its sequence, and its replacement invoice starts its own without repeating reminders already sent. **Acceptance evidence:** Age an invoice, send an authorized reminder, record a dispute then clear it and pay; verify the sequence pauses on dispute and stops on reconciled payment. Repeat with a recorded check, bounce it and verify the sequence resumes from its next due step without repeating sent reminders. Apply trust that covers one invoice in full and another in part through TRUST-004; verify the first sequence stops and the second continues for the remaining amount only. Void a reminded invoice under BILL-016 and verify its sequence stops and the rebilled invoice’s sequence starts at its first step.

**BILL-010 — Show client ledgers and receivables.** Client statements separate billed, unbilled, paid, credited, unapplied credit, disputed, trust-held, interest or late-fee and overdue amounts as of a selected date, with every balance drillable to source transactions, including offline payments, TRUST-004 trust applications shown beside their trust-ledger debits, their allocations and reversals. A BILL-016 voided invoice leaves aging and open balances and appears on the ledger beside its original issue with the void reason and its replacement invoice. Export aging by payer, matter and responsible lawyer. **Acceptance evidence:** Open a statement spanning a credit, an unapplied overpayment, a reversed check, a partial trust application and its reversal, pending ACH and trust deposit; compare as-of totals and aging to original ledger entries, see each trust application once beside its trust-ledger debit, and export them. Void one invoice and rebill it under BILL-016: aging drops the void, the ledger shows the void and its replacement once each and the as-of balance before the void is unchanged.
BILL-015 cutover is the principal’s first saved scheme.

fragments.text: **BILL-011 — Consolidate multi-matter billing.** A payer receives a consolidated invoice or statement across selected matters while each line retains matter, fee agreement, responsible attorney and permissions. Invoice recipients and view events are recorded without exposing one represented party’s privileged work to another. **Acceptance evidence:** Consolidate two matters for one client, keep a third excluded, inspect the PDF and portal view event and reconcile each matter allocation.

**BILL-012 — Record offline payments against invoices.** Billing staff record cash, check, wire or ACH received outside the processor with payer, method, check or wire reference, received and deposit dates and the operating deposit account, then allocate it across one or more of that payer’s unpaid invoices, oldest first or by explicit amounts. A short payment leaves the remainder due or, with finance approval, posts a reasoned write-off; an overpayment becomes unapplied client credit that staff later apply to another invoice or refund under BILL-007 approval. A bounced or stopped check is reversed by an append-only entry naming the original, which reopens each invoice, restores aging and resumes collection. Funds intended for trust are recorded through TRUST-002 and never applied to operating invoices directly. **Acceptance evidence:** Record one check that pays two invoices in full and a third in part, post the remainder as a write-off with finance approval and refuse an assistant’s write-off; record a second check that overpays, leaving unapplied credit, and apply that credit to the next invoice; bounce the first check and reverse it. After each step invoice status, aging, BILL-009 collection state, the BILL-010 client ledger and the BOOKS-001 QuickBooks Online sync reflect it exactly once, and replaying each request creates no second payment.

**CT policy approved with riders, 26 October 2026; implementation status unchanged.** For BILL-012 offline-payment shortfalls, finance approval means explicit approval by the active principal of the exact current invoice revision, exact positive integer USD-cent amount and recorded reason. Approval and posting retain the invoice identity and revision, amount, reason, approving person and approval time in linked append-only history. A changed revision, amount or reason requires fresh approval; current authority, matter access and ethical walls are checked at the server when posting. Billing staff may record receipts but cannot approve write-offs; lawyer, accountant or trust-officer status alone, custom roles, agent keys and integration keys confer no write-off approval authority. A write-off reduces the collectible receivable and records no payment, bank deposit or trust movement; original invoice artifacts and approvals remain unchanged. Later receipts allocate only against the remaining collectible amount, with excess retained as unapplied client credit. A bounced or stopped check reverses only the original payment allocations through linked append-only entries; it does not reverse an independently approved write-off. Invoice due, aging and collection resume only for the resulting collectible balance, without repeating sent reminders. The complete target includes a separately principal-approved, reasoned, exact-revision, append-only reversal naming the original write-off and amount, preserving both records and restoring the corresponding collectible balance exactly once. That reversal path remains a named Gap until implemented and proved. BILL-016 refuses a void while an unreversed write-off remains; until the approved reversal path is implemented and proved, such an invoice cannot be voided. Posting a write-off reversal does not bypass any existing payment-resolution, counsel-review or void prerequisite. Refunds remain subject to BILL-007 approval. This interim default does not narrow any original BILL-012 acceptance journey or the full product target. **Additional acceptance evidence required by this ruling:** Refuse write-off approval by billing staff, an assistant, a lawyer without principal authority, an accountant, a trust officer without principal authority, an agent and an integration. Approve as the active principal with the exact current invoice revision, amount and reason; inspect retained approver, approval time and linked append-only history. Refuse stale approval and posting after authority or matter access is removed. Replay the approved request without a second write-off and refuse a changed request under the same identity. Return the original check and verify that only its payment allocations reverse while the write-off remains; receive a later payment and retain any excess as unapplied client credit. Refuse a void while the write-off remains unreversed. When the reversal path is delivered, refuse unauthorized or stale reversal, approve the exact original write-off reversal as principal, retain both records, restore the collectible balance once and then re-evaluate every existing BILL-016 prerequisite. Verify restart and archive recovery and every original invoice-status, aging, collection, client-ledger and QuickBooks Online once-only obligation. Exercise changed screens with populated records at 1440 and 390 pixels. Listing this journey does not claim it passes.

**BILL-013 — Brand versioned invoice templates.** The principal or billing staff maintain firm invoice templates using FIRM-001’s logo, address and remittance details: client and matter header, payment terms and due date, payment link and QR code, and per-template choices to show or hide time-entry detail, hours, rates, timekeepers, UTBMS codes, $0 no-charge lines and discounts, a summary or detailed layout, and how trust and prior balances appear. Templates are versioned; a firm default is overridden per client or matter, and the assignment is visible in prebill review. Every issued invoice keeps its exact template revision and rendered PDF bytes, so editing or retiring a template changes only later invoices. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload a logo and remittance block, create a detailed template that shows no-charge lines and a summary template that hides hours and rates, and assign each to a different matter; issue both invoices and inspect the PDFs for logo, remittance block, header, terms, trust balance and the chosen detail. Edit the detailed template and issue a new invoice; the earlier PDF downloads byte-identical and names the earlier revision.

**BILL-014 — Charge interest and late fees by agreement.** Firms configure per-client or per-matter payment profiles with terms, grace period, simple interest rate or flat late fee. Satchel refuses a charge the signed engagement terms do not authorize. Due charges are calculated in exact cents from the as-of unpaid balance and appear as draft lines for billing review before posting; they never accrue on trust balances, disputed amounts or installments current under a BILL-008 payment plan. Waivers carry a reason and finance approval. **Acceptance evidence:** Set 30-day terms, a 10-day grace period and 1% monthly simple interest on one matter and none on another; age both invoices past grace, review and post interest on the first only; record a partial offline payment and inspect the next accrual on the reduced balance; mark the invoice disputed and see accrual stop; waive one charge with approval and refuse an assistant’s waiver.

**BILL-015 — Number invoices by firm scheme.** The principal configures the invoice-number pattern from a starting number, padding, prefix, year and separators. Each issued invoice receives the next unique number atomically, even within a concurrent batch; drafts and returned prebills consume no number, and an invoice voided under BILL-016 keeps its number, which is never reissued, while its rebill receives the next number. After a move, numbering continues from a firm-set next number above the last imported source invoice number, and imported invoices keep their source numbers (MOVE-002–007) without collision; a pattern change applies only to later invoices. **Acceptance evidence:** Import Clio invoices through 2024-0187, set the next number to 2024-0188 and issue two invoices concurrently in one batch, receiving 2024-0188 and 2024-0189; return a prebill and confirm it consumed no number; refuse a next number that collides with an imported invoice; void 2024-0189 under BILL-016 and rebill its entries, receiving 2024-0190 while 2024-0189 stays on the voided invoice; change the prefix and verify issued PDFs, the BILL-010 ledger and QuickBooks Online sync keep their original numbers. BILL-015 cutover is the principal’s first saved scheme. Every pre-cutover number and approved/exported file stays byte-identical; a legacy draft with a reservation issues under that same number. Later drafts have only their ID and a non-invoice label. Number assignment, exact approved-revision and tax gates, PDF and LEDES rendering, permanent firm-wide registration and counter advance form one atomic issue operation; a failed batch consumes none, collisions are refused rather than skipped, and no gap-free claim is made. Scheme versions apply only to later issues; year is from issue time in the firm IANA timezone and a counter reset requires an explicit noncolliding next number. Corrections retain <original>-R<k> without advancing the counter. Imports preserve source numbers and provenance with the next counter above every source ordinal; restore retains the register, counter and files. A legacy reserved draft approved after the first saved scheme keeps its reserved number and must pass atomic issue before export. A concurrent issue conflict commits no number; refreshing and replaying the exact approved issue request reconciles the durable result. Already frozen legacy artifacts remain byte-identical.

**BILL-016 — Void issued invoices and rebill their entries.** A lawyer, or billing staff with finance approval, voids an approved or issued invoice with a recorded reason; assistants and agents never void, and an agent may only propose a void for a person to decide. Satchel refuses the void while the invoice carries an offline BILL-012 payment, a LawPay or Stripe BILL-005/BILL-006 payment or a TRUST-004 trust application, until each is reversed, refunded or moved to unapplied client credit by an append-only entry naming the original. The void is itself an append-only record: the original invoice, its BILL-013 template revision, line artifacts and PDF stay downloadable byte-identical beside a void notice in the invoice record and listings, its BILL-015 number is kept and never reissued, a voided invoice cannot be restored, and replaying the void request changes nothing. The void releases the invoice’s source reservations, so its time and expense entries return to unbilled; authorized staff then correct narrative, rate, UTBMS code or template assignment, or move an entry to another matter of the same client, with field-level edit history, and a moved entry takes the target matter’s access and ethical-wall rules. Each released entry is rebilled exactly once, on a new invoice with a new BILL-015 number and any BILL-013 template. Downstream, BILL-009 stops chasing the voided invoice; BILL-010 aging drops it while the client ledger shows the void beside the original; the invoice’s portal page, payment link, text-to-pay link and QR code refuse payment and name the replacement; BILL-014 interest stops accruing on it; BOOKS-001 voids the QuickBooks Online invoice exactly once; and REPORT-002 counts each entry’s billed value once, from the live invoice. SAT-006 correction deltas remain the way to adjust an amount without releasing entries. The current native edit door retains the source ID, creator, work date, worked duration and expense cost. A changed explicit hourly rate replaces the recorded price using worked minutes × hourly USD cents / 60, rounded half-up to cents, without a discount or agreement increment; an unchanged rate retains its recorded pricing. Narrative and UTBMS edits do not reprice. Moving preserves that recorded price and requires current access to both matters and their same recorded client value, as used by native client fee agreements. Each edit binds the reviewed entry revision and reason, records before/after values and actor, and refuses while the entry is reserved in another bill. Current entry-matter access controls its edit history; moving work grants no document or receipt access. **Acceptance evidence:** Issue and send a two-entry invoice; refuse a void by an assistant and by an agent key. Record a partial check against it under BILL-012 and receive refusal of the void; reverse the payment to unapplied credit. Void it as billing staff with finance approval and a reason: the original PDF downloads byte-identical, marked void in its record, with its number unchanged, and a repeated void request changes nothing. Its payment link and portal pay button refuse payment and BILL-009 stops its sequence. Move one entry to the client’s other matter and correct the other entry’s narrative, then read both entries’ edit history. Rebill both matters: each entry appears on exactly one live invoice under a new BILL-015 number, a second rebill of either entry is refused, and the unapplied credit applies to one new invoice. BILL-010 aging, the client ledger, REPORT-002 billed and realization totals and the BOOKS-001 QuickBooks Online sync show the void and the two new invoices once each, and replaying the void and the sync creates nothing new.
BILL-015 cutover is the principal’s first saved scheme.

fragments.text: A BILL-012 write-off is independent of payment reversal: refuse a void while any write-off remains unreversed, and permit further void review only after its separately principal-approved append-only reversal has posted; until that reversal path is implemented and proved, the written-off invoice remains ineligible for void.

**TRUST-001 — Keep built-in IOLTA client ledgers.** Satchel itself maintains separate US IOLTA/trust bank registers, client/matter subsidiary ledgers and operating records in exact cents. Opening balances require dated source statements and approval; a shared bank balance never substitutes for each client’s owned funds. Native openings retain the exact document version and SHA-256 reviewed by the designated trust officer. Dates are inclusive YYYY-MM-DD calendar dates; future statement dates are refused against the current UTC date. Operating openings have no trust subsidiary; each trust opening belongs to one matter ledger. **Acceptance evidence:** Create an IOLTA account and two client ledgers, import reviewed opening balances and drill bank and client totals to their source records.

**TRUST-002 — Record deposits and disbursements.** Record trust receipts, retainer deposits, checks, wires and authorized disbursements with payer/payee, matter, bank reference, deposit/cleared dates and supporting documents. Unidentified receipts remain suspense items rather than another client’s available money. A native posting records bank activity and never claims to send money. Dates are inclusive YYYY-MM-DD dates ordered received ≤ deposit/payment ≤ cleared; future UTC dates and new transaction posting dates before the bank register’s latest posting are refused. **Acceptance evidence:** Deposit funds for two clients, record a third unidentified receipt and disburse a cleared authorized amount; inspect separate balances and a suspense exception.

**TRUST-003 — Prevent overdrafts and commingling.** Trust availability is calculated per client/matter and cleared funds, with pending commitments included. Refuse negative balances, cross-client borrowing, fee deductions from principal and unsupported backdating; exceptions cannot be hidden by editing history. **Acceptance evidence:** Attempt a transfer exceeding one client’s cleared balance while the bank has sufficient aggregate cash; refuse it and retain the attempted-action history.

**TRUST-004 — Authorize earned-fee trust transfers.** A designated trust officer approves a reviewed earned invoice and exact available client funds for trust-to-operating transfer. Dual authorization is configurable; bank or processor execution and actual cleared results reconcile before balances are final. Agents never authorize movement. Billing staff request the application during BILL-001 prebill or batch approval or against an already issued invoice by choosing the client’s trust ledger as that invoice’s payment source; the request reserves the funds under TRUST-003 until the officer approves or declines it. Each approved application posts paired, linked entries exactly once: a debit on the client’s matter trust ledger and trust bank register, and an operating payment allocated to the invoice. The invoice becomes paid when the application covers it; when cleared trust falls short, Satchel applies only the available amount, never overdraws the client ledger and leaves the remainder due in aging. The application stops or reduces BILL-009 collection, appears once on the BILL-010 client ledger beside its trust-ledger debit, in the client trust statement and in the TRUST-005 register, and syncs to BOOKS-001 as one operating payment, never as a second deposit or an untouched receivable. A mistaken application is reversed by an append-only entry naming the original, which reopens the invoice by the reversed amount and restores the client’s trust balance. **Acceptance evidence:** Issue a $1,000 and a $900 invoice to a client holding $1,500 in cleared trust; request trust application to the first during BILL-001 batch approval and to the second after issue, and refuse an assistant’s or agent’s approval. The trust officer approves both, with a second approver while dual authorization is on; interrupt execution and reconcile its bank reference. The first invoice is paid and the second shows $500 paid and $400 due in aging. The trust ledger, trust bank register, client trust statement, BILL-010 ledger and TRUST-005 register each show each application once; BILL-009 stops the first invoice’s sequence and continues the second’s for $400; BOOKS-001 posts one QuickBooks Online operating payment per application, and replaying either approval creates nothing new. Reverse the second application by an append-only entry: the invoice reopens to $900 due, the client’s trust balance returns to $500 and the reversal syncs once. TIME-005 execution obligation: settlement disbursement preparation and final approval bind the exact current settlement revision, allocation, payee and amount to its required counsel and designated trust-officer approvals, including any valid recorded sole-practitioner setting. Recheck current authority, ethical walls and cleared unreserved same-matter availability at execution. A TIME-005 readiness result supplies no spending approval or reservation. Preserve the existing transfer, posting, uncertain-result and bank-reconciliation controls.

**TRUST-005 — Reconcile all three trust views.** For each statement period reconcile adjusted bank statement balance, trust bank register and sum of client subsidiary balances, showing outstanding checks/deposits and every difference. A trust officer signs and locks a dated reconciliation packet only when differences are resolved or explicitly recorded for correction. Amounts are exact integer USD cents. Statement import retains the uploaded bank original, version and hash with the officer-recorded closing balance; TRUST-007 adds bank-row parsing and feeds. The inclusive effective-date cutoff adds outstanding deposits and subtracts outstanding checks from the statement balance; the register includes suspense while the subsidiary sum excludes it. Each difference links to its entries and original sources. A signed packet freezes the report, client statements, source references, actor, time and SHA-256 digest. **Acceptance evidence:** Import a bank statement with an outstanding check and a misallocated receipt, inspect three-way differences, correct by journal and sign a balanced packet. Run consecutive monthly periods and compare all three balances in integer cents. Drill a $12.50 difference to its misallocated receipt and an outstanding check to its bank/register entries, resolve the discrepancy and verify all three adjusted totals agree to the cent before the balanced packet is signed.

**TRUST-006 — Correct and lock trust history.** Posted trust entries are append-only; reversals name the original and reason, closed periods need authorized reopen, and each action retains person/time/source. Reconciliation reports and client trust statements reproduce any prior cutoff. Cutoffs include all entries effective on or before the selected calendar date. Current reports include later-recorded corrections, while each signed packet and its client statements retain their original frozen version and SHA-256 digest. An active documented reopen permits historical correcting entries within that period even after later postings; every other signed cutoff that would change must also be reopened. Historical debits and receipt reversals must preserve nonnegative cleared balances at every intervening effective/clearance date, so later deposits cannot finance an earlier payment. Journal reversals correct ledger records and never claim to move money; earned-fee applications retain TRUST-004’s bank-confirmed return process. **Acceptance evidence:** Reverse a misallocated deposit after month-end, require authorized reopen and compare the original signed packet with the corrected version and full trail.

**TRUST-007 — Match banks and legal processor settlements.** Import OFX/QFX or bank CSV statements and connect authorized US bank feeds such as Plaid, matching LawPay/Stripe settlement references without duplicating receipts. Trust and operating feeds remain separate, with unresolved matches and stale-feed status visible. **Acceptance evidence:** Import a statement twice, match a processor batch and one outstanding deposit, then disconnect the feed; verify one transaction per source and an unresolved stale-state banner.

**TRUST-008 — Report trust and replenish retainers.** Trust officers and authorized clients obtain client trust statements, balance alerts, reconciliation packets and state trust-record reports reviewed by the firm. California (Rule 1.15 monthly reconciliation of client ledgers, account journal and bank statements, and Client Trust Account Protection Program annual reporting fields) and New York (Rule 1.15(d) required bookkeeping records, retained seven years) ship first; other states’ fields are configured and reviewed by the firm. Low retainers generate approved replenishment requests; they never auto-withdraw funds without valid authorization. **Acceptance evidence:** Generate a monthly trust packet and client statement, produce the California monthly reconciliation and New York required-records report for the same period and trace each required field to source entries, cross a retainer threshold and inspect a delivered replenishment request without any unauthorized debit. **Conservative implementation default, pending ct approval:** Only the active native principal, with existing trust-record authority and full account access, explicitly releases an exact current officer-signed ledger statement to one current client or co-client grant. Payers and delegates receive no trust statements or replenishment requests. The principal approves versioned retainer thresholds; a principal who is also a designated trust officer approves the exact current posted-balance alert before publishing a replenishment request to one current client or co-client grant. Delivery means authenticated portal publication only, with an audited timestamp; it sends no email or SMS, initiates no provider call and never authorizes or posts a debit. Reads recheck the original recipient grant, active principal authorizer and ethical walls; a fresh grant cannot revive old publication authority. Statement release and request-delivery authority are excluded from archive restore, while signed records, policy versions and immutable audit evidence remain recoverable. State-record downloads are incomplete review previews, not compliance certifications or annual filings. CLIENT-001 grant rules and existing trust-record authority continue to apply. This default changes no acceptance sentence and is not a DONE claim.

**TRUST-009 — Produce checks and deposit records.** Authorized staff prepare numbered trust/operating checks and deposit slips tied to approved ledger transactions, support void/reissue with reasons and bank matching, and prevent duplicate check numbers or printing from authorizing a payment. The principal with an active trust-officer designation records operating transactions; designated trust officers with current matter access prepare trust checks. Numbering accepts 1–12 positive decimal input digits and canonicalizes leading zeros and is unique per bank account forever, including voided checks. A printable check requires an approved, uncleared check disbursement. A void names a reason, exact check revision and supporting original and posts only after an officer reviews the exact reversal; pending/approved voids prevent clearance, and cleared checks require bank reversal rather than a void. A replacement requires a separately approved matching account, client ledger, payee and amount, with a new number linked to the approved void. Bank matching records the exact check number, amount, bank reference and source-backed cleared date without claiming a Satchel bank send. Deposit slips contain distinct approved uncleared receipts from one account, keep source references and say they are a record rather than bank confirmation; printing never posts or approves. Operating receipts and payments have no client subsidiary; cleared operating availability deducts pending operating payments and earned-fee reversals, and every posting preserves nonnegative historical balances. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a reviewed disbursement check, void and reissue it, reconcile the bank debit and inspect both numbers and unchanged client ownership.

**TRUST-010 — Transfer trust between one client’s matters.** A trust officer moves cleared funds between two matter ledgers of the same client, such as a closed matter’s remaining retainer to that client’s new matter, with a reason, the client’s written authorization attached and optional dual approval. Within one trust bank account the transfer posts one paired, append-only debit and credit, so the bank register is unchanged and TRUST-005 stays balanced; a move between two trust bank accounts also records and reconciles the bank movement. Transfers to another client, of uncleared funds or above the source matter’s available balance are refused under TRUST-003. Same client means the same canonical INTAKE-004 party related as client on both matters, including retained merged IDs; matching free-text client names never establishes identity. Each designated officer must currently see both matters. The request pins the written authorization’s retained matter-visible document version and hash, reason, exact cents, ledger pair and transfer date; a later document version does not rewrite that authority, while erasure or lost visibility refuses further work. Request keys replay exactly without another allocation. The firm’s one/two-distinct-officer approval policy is frozen on request; approvals must still be active before posting or bank submission. Within one account, final approval atomically posts opposite cleared subsidiary entries; bank-register rows exclude these allocations while both client statements and three-way totals retain them. Between accounts, approval only reserves: a person records submitted and then cleared or confirmed-not-executed bank outcomes, with exact debit/credit amounts, references, dates and originals for both accounts. Uncertain submission retains the reservation across restart; only cleared evidence posts the paired bank entries, once, and no Satchel bank send is claimed. Reversals require written authority and at least the original or current stronger approval threshold, name the original transfer and append its opposite pair; generic one-sided clearance/reversal refuses these entries. Available cleared funds include pending reservations from every disbursement, earned-fee application and matter-transfer door. Signed periods still require explicit reopening before a correction; their signed packets remain immutable. **Acceptance evidence:** Close a matter holding $750 in trust, attach the client’s authorization and transfer $750 to the same client’s new matter; inspect paired matter-ledger entries, an unchanged bank register, both client trust statements and a balanced TRUST-005 view; refuse a transfer to another client’s matter and one exceeding cleared funds; replay the approval without a second transfer, then reverse it by an append-only entry naming the original.

**BOOKS-001 — Synchronize QuickBooks Online operations.** Map clients, matters/classes, operating invoices, payments (processor payments, offline BILL-012 payments and TRUST-004 trust applications, each as one operating payment with its invoice allocations), credits and credit applications, write-offs, reversals, expenses, fees and tax to QuickBooks Online with stable external IDs, direction/ownership settings and conflict queues. Trust liability summaries are explicitly mapped and never mistaken for operating revenue; a trust application never posts as a second deposit or leaves its receivable open. A BILL-016 void voids the matching QuickBooks Online invoice exactly once and each rebill syncs as a new invoice under its new number. **Acceptance evidence:** Sync an operating invoice, partial payment, fee and credit twice, then a check applied across two invoices and its reversal, and a trust application to an invoice and its reversal; edit a conflicting QBO record and reconcile totals through a visible conflict queue with one QBO payment per Satchel payment or trust application and no duplicate deposit. Void a synced invoice and rebill it, replay the sync and see one voided and one new QBO invoice.
BILL-015 cutover is the principal’s first saved scheme.
