fragments.text: **BOOKS-002 — Synchronize Xero operations.** Xero is a supported alternative for contacts, operating invoices, payments, credit notes, expenses and account mappings with idempotent references and reconciliation. A firm chooses one accounting source per entity; trust subsidiary ledgers remain in Satchel. **Acceptance evidence:** Sync an invoice and refund, return a provider validation error, repair its account mapping and reconcile one correct record per transaction.
**CONNECT-001 — Expose scoped APIs and webhooks.**

Documented versioned APIs and signed webhooks expose permitted matters, tasks, documents, deadlines and finance events with pagination, scopes, idempotency and delivery journals. Agent credentials cannot approve legal work, move funds or escalate their own access. The principal creates each integration with an explicit existing-matter allow-list and per-resource read capabilities; each read and delivery intersects those with the sponsor’s current active access and document ACL. A preparation capability creates only matter-bound bill/deadline proposals, with an atomic request-key replay record; SAT-009 keeps its separate new-matter preparation door. Only the principal may enter a webhook destination. The current outbound rule checks HTTPS on port 443, rejects credentials/fragments, reserved hostnames and non-public literal addresses, and uses Workers fetch with redirects refused. There is no separate DNS preflight and no application address pin; resolved-address/pinned egress remains the named Base egress-door Gap, and CONNECT-001 stays partial until adoption. FIRM-004 declares this metadata-only outbound flow and inherits the same named gap. Opt-in metadata events contain only stable IDs, type and time; HMAC-SHA256 covers attempt Unix seconds, event ID and exact body. Receivers use a five-minute replay window and deduplicate by event ID; at-least-once delivery never claims exactly-once processing. Every attempt is journaled; five consecutive failed or uncertain deliveries pause until principal resumption. Rotating credentials replaces the API key and sealed signing secret, invalidates the old key and pauses delivery while the receiver changes its secret; revocation stops new claims while an already claimed request may have reached its destination. Secrets and credential-bound queues are installation-local and absent from archive/API listings; the normal action audit retains safe outcomes.
**Acceptance evidence:** Create a scoped integration, page permitted matters, receive a signed event twice and refuse access to another matter and an approval route.

**CONNECT-002 — Connect Zapier and Clio APIs.** Zapier triggers/actions and an authorized Clio API connector route external intake and approved case updates through the same validation, conflict and permission doors. Connector status, duplicates, rate limits and revocation are visible without silently dropping work. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive a Zapier lead and a Clio update twice, map them to one matter record, hit a provider rate limit and revoke the grant with queued work visible.

**CONNECT-003 — Reconcile connector work durably.** Every connector exposes last successful sync, queued work, source IDs, attempts, replies, next action and completion evidence. Restart resumes durable state; uncertain non-idempotent sends wait for reconciliation or a human, and permission changes stop unauthorized queued actions. The current native scoped API/webhook connector keeps durable source event IDs and delivery attempts across worker restarts. Its journal shows queued work, source matter/record/event IDs, last receiver HTTP acceptance, principal-recorded confirmation, response status, attempts, completion evidence and each next action. A 3xx/4xx reply is a failed attempt; a 5xx reply, connection interruption or expired sending lease is uncertain and never retried automatically. The principal resolves the exact latest uncertain attempt using an external reference and receiver evidence: received closes it without another send, while not received permits a later attempt only under current access. This is human-recorded evidence, never independent provider verification or proof of downstream completion. Removing a matter from the integration’s existing allow-list immediately refuses its API reads and queued work; each claim checks the current integration generation. An already-sending request may have reached the receiver and remains visible for reconciliation. Reconciliation history and safe audit evidence restore without credentials or credential-bound queues. Every capability that exists today conforms; FIRM-004, INTAKE-006/009, DOC-005/007/008/009/010/011, CAL-002/003/004/005/009/010, CLIENT-005/006/007, TIME-002/006, BILL-005/006/007/008, TRUST-007, BOOKS-001/002, CONNECT-002, MOVE-008 and AGENT-002/003/004 and every future connector inherit these obligations before shipping. CONNECT-001 remains partial for its separate Base resolved-address/pinned-egress gap. **Acceptance evidence:** Interrupt a provider response and restart, reconcile by external reference, then revoke matter access and verify blocked queued work and no duplicate external effect.

**REPORT-001 — Report case status and outcomes.** Dashboards filter active/closed matters, stage duration, outcomes, lead conversion, evidence gaps, deadlines and workload by practice, owner and date. Every count drills into permitted records and exports the same filtered data. The principal and lawyers use seven Reports dashboards and the same filtered source rows for counts, drill-downs and CSV. Current matter grants apply before every dataset (including converted leads), count, drill and export; an ungranted matter is the current exclusion acceptance case. FIRM-003 inherits exclusion of a principal outside an ethical wall, and FIRM-008 inherits finer report scopes, before those capabilities ship. Matter cohorts filter by exact practice, responsible stage-profile lawyer, open/closed status and inclusive opened calendar dates in the firm timezone (UTC before setup). Lead cohorts use assignee and inclusive received dates; merged duplicates are excluded, converted leads linked to inaccessible matters are excluded, and unclassified leads remain a distinct No practice bucket in conversion denominators even with a named practice filter. The case-status filter applies only to matters. Conversion is converted divided by all counted leads. Practice is an explicit configured code on native lead creation/update and the versioned intake form; submissions copy the saved code without inferring it from free text. Stage duration sums successful transition intervals while open, pauses at closure and resumes at reopening; days mean 86,400,000 elapsed milliseconds, displayed half-up to two decimals, with exact milliseconds in CSV. Unassigned or unrecorded stage history is labelled, never inferred from a profile edit. On closing, the principal or responsible lawyer must record won, settled, lost, dismissed, withdrawn, transactional complete, or other with details, atomically beside the immutable closure event; older closed matters show Outcome not recorded and nothing is inferred from a closure reason. Reopening retains the prior attributed outcome in history; open matters do not count as completed outcomes. Missing evidence counts only reader-visible retained current originals of each current stage-required type. Deadlines include proposed/confirmed dates and exclude superseded/completed dates; workload includes open tasks and those deadlines, with overdue strictly before the firm-local today. An open task linked to a superseded date remains work labelled for review, without treating that obsolete date as current overdue work. Exports reapply the same filters and current permissions, include exact source identifiers and add an audit action; export never widens access. **Acceptance evidence:** Filter an attorney’s litigation cohort, trace an overdue count to its matters and export matching rows without a walled case appearing.

**REPORT-002 — Report firm economics.** Show utilization, realization, collection rate, effective rate, billed/unbilled work, WIP, aging and matter profitability with explicit formulas, approved staff cost rates and as-of dates. Distinguish pending payments, trust cash and earned revenue. A BILL-016 void and its rebill count each entry’s billed value once, from the live invoice, so billed totals and realization never double-count them. **Acceptance evidence:** Follow one time entry through write-down, invoice, partial settlement and expense; reconcile each report to source transactions and export the formula basis. Void that invoice and rebill the entry at a corrected rate; billed, realization and collection totals count the entry once at the corrected value.

**CT policy ruling, 26 October 2026 — approved with riders; implementation status unchanged.** Staff cost entry, approval and version management, and economics reads and exports, require an active human native session whose current firm membership has the principal role. Initial principal authority comes from native firm setup; later grants and removals use the existing principal-controlled membership process and its audit. An administrator title, lawyer role, accountant role, manager title, custom role, agent sponsorship or provider account ownership does not confer this authority. Deactivation, role removal or session revocation ends access on the next request, including download requests. Historical approvals retain their original actor and time.

A principal enters an explicit hourly staff cost in exact USD cents for an identified timekeeper and effective work date, records its basis and approves the exact saved revision. The same principal may enter and approve it; independent second approval is not claimed. Draft or unapproved costs never enter profitability. Changes create append-only versions with author, approver, timestamps and effective dates; ambiguous overlapping approved versions are refused. Billing rates, invoices and later membership changes never supply or infer a staff cost. A retroactive approved version may change a newly generated calculation, but cannot rewrite an earlier exported artifact or its recorded basis.

Principals may inspect and export utilization, realization, collection rate, effective rate, billed and unbilled work, WIP, aging and matter profitability only within current matter permissions and ethical walls. Every metric discloses its formula, units, numerator, denominator, source identifiers, relevant revisions, filters, calculation time and supported as-of basis. Current-state results are labeled current-state; unsupported historical as-of requests are refused. Recorded-time utilization means billable recorded minutes divided by all recorded minutes in the same permitted cohort and period; it is not staff capacity, attendance or unrecorded work. A zero denominator yields unknown, not zero.

Profitability identifies the revenue basis and included staff costs and expenses. Every required time-cost component must have an applicable approved cost version. Otherwise the affected profitability is unknown, including any aggregate requiring that component; missing costs are never zero, inferred from billing prices or estimated as fact. An explicitly approved zero cost remains distinguishable from missing cost. Partial coverage may be shown separately with its coverage and exclusions, never labeled complete profitability. Pending payments, trust cash and earned revenue remain distinct. Voids, corrections, reversals and rebills retain source links and count their economic effect once.

Non-principals, agent keys, integrations, clients and payers receive neither staff cost records nor REPORT-002 economics through any read, search, count, drill, option, export or indirect response. FIRM-008 continues to own broader manager reporting scopes within built-in authority, grants and walls; it cannot widen this principal-only default. New economics doors inherit its server-door map before shipping.

An export is an explicit principal download, not external delivery. Authorization, current principal membership, matter access and walls are rechecked when generating and downloading it. Each export carries a confidential internal-use marking and a manifest identifying the firm, requesting actor, generation time, filters, supported as-of basis, formulas, source and cost-version basis, missing-data coverage and artifact hash. Custody is audited. Marking records custody and does not prevent copying. No public link or durable bearer authority is created. Staff costs, economics values, formula-basis payloads and their artifacts are excluded from email, SMS, portal summaries, webhooks, connected repositories, provider synchronization and agent or model context. This clause authorizes no sending, charging, payment approval or money movement.

Native archives preserve cost versions, approvals and export custody records under existing archive authorization and wall restrictions, without importing identities, sessions, credentials or authority grants. Restore validates integrity, retains imported history unchanged and appends a custody action; current authority is checked afresh. External effects remain paused under FIRM-007. Audit records cover cost entry, approval, supersession, export requests and outcomes, with immutable actor and revision evidence; unauthorized readers receive no cost payload through audit.

Applicable FIRM-006 holds block ordinary erasure and scheduled disposal. Approved disposal removes covered cost payloads and retained report derivatives or artifacts, records affected kinds and counts, and preserves only the permitted minimal audit and erasure evidence. Later erasure journals fence older archives against resurrection. Previously downloaded copies remain outside local erasure. Retention periods and lawful processing bases are firm decisions; this policy certifies neither compensation-law nor accounting compliance.

**REPORT-003 — Schedule actionable reports.** Authorized principals save practice-specific reports and schedule permissioned email/portal summaries with sensitive data minimization, delivery status and a due owner action for exceptions. Saved reports preserve definitions and filters across export. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule a weekly overdue-work report, revoke a recipient and verify future delivery excludes them and failed delivery creates an actionable exception.

**MOBILE-001 — Complete practice work on phones.** Responsive desktop and phone interfaces and supported iOS/Android apps cover matter lookup, documents, camera scans, time, calendar, messages and approvals with the same role controls,
and meet WCAG 2.2 AA, including complete keyboard and screen-reader (VoiceOver, TalkBack, NVDA) navigation.
**Acceptance evidence:** At 1440 and 390 pixels and on iOS/Android, find a real matter, scan a record, capture time, read a client reply and approve allowed work without clipping or lost state.
An automated axe-core pass reports no WCAG 2.2 AA violations on every workspace tab, and the matter, time and approval journeys complete by keyboard alone and with VoiceOver and TalkBack.

**MOBILE-002 — Protect offline work and push alerts.** Explicitly enabled encrypted device caches show freshness and restrict confidential previews; offline time/notes queue visibly and resolve conflicts on reconnect. Push alerts honor confidentiality and device revocation, which removes local authority and cached data when the device reconnects. **Acceptance evidence:** Record time offline, change the matter on desktop, reconnect and resolve the conflict; revoke the phone and inspect cache and push access.

**MOVE-001 — Preview and reconcile a whole firm move.** The principal previews source-specific packages with schema/version, mapping, record counts, files/hashes, relationships, rejections and coverage gaps before any write. Apply is resumable and idempotent; undo preserves records changed or used natively. Cutover requires signed reconciliation and a final delta. **Acceptance evidence:** Preview a multi-matter export, repair an unmatched client and missing file, apply twice with interruption and undo safe rows; sign cutover only after source counts and balances reconcile.

**MOVE-002 — Migrate Clio Manage and Grow completely.** Import Clio Manage/Grow contacts, matters, relationships, notes, time/expenses, tasks, email/call records, calendar CSV/ICS, invoices with their numbers and AR/trust balances using native CSV/API and separately exported or escrowed originals, including each historic bill’s original invoice PDF, attached to its matter and invoice record as evidence that staff can open and re-send to the client. Preserve source IDs, custom fields and staff mappings; retrieve missing history through authorized API/vendor-assisted extraction before cutover. **Acceptance evidence:** Move two active and one closed Clio matters plus a Grow lead, compare files and dates, reconcile billed/unbilled and client trust totals, open a historic Clio invoice’s original PDF from its matter and re-send it through the portal with byte-identical content, and prove repeat import creates no duplicates.
BILL-015 cutover is the principal’s first saved scheme.

fragments.text: **MOVE-008 — Prove finance and authority at cutover.** For every source distinguish dated opening balances from full historical transactions, reconcile WIP, AR, credits and trust per client/matter/bank, and preserve supporting statements. Reauthorize mail, calendars, processors, accounting, portal users and signature providers; do not import passwords, payment tokens or live sends as authority. Because payment tokens never move, cutover runs a guided re-consent campaign: Satchel lists every client with an active source payment plan or saved-card autopay (including Clio Payments plans) with its next installment date, sends each an authorized re-authorization link under LawPay or Stripe through CLIENT-006 or CLIENT-005, keeps each imported BILL-008 plan paused with an owner task due before its next installment, and resumes the plan only on the client’s recorded consent. **Acceptance evidence:** Shadow a billing/trust period against source reports, find a missing payment, repair it and approve cutover; restored queues remain paused and connector work needs new authorization. Import two Clio Payments plans, send both re-authorization links, record one client’s consent and see that plan charge its next installment once; the other plan stays paused and its owner task becomes overdue before its installment date. Introduce a $12.50 client trust mismatch and refuse cutover approval; show the exact source and destination ledger difference, repair it with provenance, and permit switching only when every client/matter/bank trust total agrees to the cent.

**AGENT-001 — Build evidence-closed matter plans.** The matter agent reads permitted engagement terms, orders, correspondence, records and workflow dependencies to maintain an editable obligations map with milestone, evidence needed, owner, next due action and completion criteria. Counsel approves legal interpretation; no milestone closes because a job merely ran. **Acceptance evidence:** Give an active matter a missing witness statement, review the proposed plan, upload an unrelated file and keep the milestone open; accept the right evidence and inspect its source-linked completion. Give the agent an approved claim with required elements, inspect its file-to-claim evidence map and cited source pages, and identify the missing bank record explicitly; an unrelated upload cannot satisfy that claim element.

**AGENT-002 — Chase authorized evidence to acceptance.** Within a delegated recipient/channel/time/contact budget, the agent requests missing client/provider records, handles replies and routine calls through contracted Twilio/voice services, files returned originals and asks staff to accept sufficiency. Expired authority, failed contact, legal uncertainty or a limit stops and escalates. **Acceptance evidence:** Authorize one provider request and a bounded chase, return a partial record, reach the contact limit and inspect escalation; accept the final record and verify all future chases stop. Request a missing client bank statement through CLIENT-003 in the authenticated portal and an authorized bank/provider request within the delegation; track each recipient, reply, deficiency and accepted original separately and stop both chases once their evidence is accepted.

**AGENT-003 — Explain deadline changes before propagation.** The agent compares source passages in incoming orders and rule-provider changes, proposes dependent dates/tasks and staffing, and awaits attorney confirmation of every legal change before reconciling calendar delivery and acknowledgments. It exposes uncertainty and superseded sources. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive an amended order, inspect cited old/new passages, reject one inferred deadline, approve another and verify only the approved change reaches each calendar with acknowledgment status.

**AGENT-004 — Draft substantive work with verified sources.** Using authorized matter evidence, approved templates and licensed research access such as Westlaw, LexisNexis or vLex, the agent drafts demands, complaints, discovery, deposition outlines and responses. Each factual/legal proposition links to source version/page or licensed authority; unsupported assertions remain flagged and lawyers approve all external work. **Acceptance evidence:** Draft a demand and discovery response from mixed records, open factual citations, flag an unsupported allegation and unavailable authority, revise with counsel and prove nothing sends or files before approval.

**AGENT-005 — Review active matters every night.** A scheduled agent checks permitted active matters for missing evidence, treatment/billing gaps, approaching limitations, stalled work and inconsistent facts, producing ranked next actions with exact sources and a responsible person. Counsel tunes practice-specific policy, suppresses false positives and chooses execution scope. **Acceptance evidence:** Run overnight on three matters including a treatment gap and completed request; inspect source-linked proposed actions, suppress one and verify the next run preserves the decision without duplicate tasks.

**AGENT-006 — Reconcile matter work to collected cash.** The agent joins permitted document/email activity, confirmed time, fee agreements, costs, bills, settlements and books to find unbilled work or payment mismatches. Timekeepers confirm billability, counsel reviews bills and finance alone authorizes transfers, refunds and write-offs; the agent pursues only approved collection actions. **Acceptance evidence:** Detect worked-but-unbilled email and an unmatched settlement, review each recommendation and reconcile the final invoice/payment; refuse an agent attempt to approve or transfer trust funds.

**AGENT-007 — Keep client promises through delivery.** From approved updates the agent extracts a reviewed promise and date, tracks underlying tasks and evidence, prompts the owner before a miss and prepares the next source-cited update. Counsel approves wording, privilege and recipients; delivery and replies are reconciled before the promise closes. Before shipping, its reviewed promises participate in MATTER-007’s live closure inventory, remaining unresolved until evidenced fulfillment or an individual counsel carry decision; reopening restores only explicitly approved workflows and existing access. **Acceptance evidence:** Approve a promise to deliver a draft Friday, delay its dependency, inspect an owner escalation and approve a revised update; verify receipt and retain the original promise history.

**AGENT-008 — Coordinate milestones with billing and collection.** The agent coordinates editable practice workflows across accepted evidence, confirmed deadlines, reviewable deliverables, earned billing and authorized collection until each milestone’s legal and financial conditions are satisfied. It keeps separate owners and approvals, durable attempts and stop controls; a payment never substitutes for unfinished legal work. **Acceptance evidence:** Run a demand milestone from missing records through attorney-approved draft and earned invoice, return the payment and confirm the legal work stays complete while the collection obligation reopens.

**AGENT-009 — Measure recovered work and agent decisions.** Principals inspect completed milestones, recovered billable work, time saved using a disclosed baseline, overdue reductions, source accuracy and human overrides. Every recommendation shows data used, policy/model revision and decision; metrics never reward false completion or expose walled matters. **Acceptance evidence:** Compare an agent-assisted cohort against the chosen baseline, drill a recovered-time metric to confirmed work and inspect rejected recommendations and excluded restricted matters.
**AGENT-010 — Constrain agent data and execution.** Agents use only authorized matter and licensed research context under firm-approved retention/training and health-data agreements;
untrusted documents and messages cannot grant authority.

Delegations specify permitted actions, recipients, spend, expiry and stop/escalation rules; revocation cancels queued authority while retaining outcome history. **Acceptance evidence:** Embed a send-and-transfer instruction in an uploaded record, revoke the delegation before scheduled work and inspect refusal, redacted context and preserved proposal history without an external effect.

Satchel is US-first and uses USD by default. Licensed lawyers decide legal interpretation, conflicts, advice, filings and jurisdiction-specific professional duties. The software supports evidence, review and execution controls; it does not act as counsel or guarantee conflict clearance. Licensed Westlaw/LexisNexis/vLex access supplies external legal authority; restricted licensed content is not silently copied or redistributed.

A regulated US bank owns each IOLTA/operating account. LawPay or a firm-verified Stripe arrangement processes payments; provider onboarding, trust protections, ACH authorization and bank agreements are required engineering and setup, not excluded scope. Satchel still owns the complete legal ledger, approval workflow, three-way reconciliation and discrepancy resolution. It neither takes custody of client money nor claims that a payment request is settlement.

LawToolBox/CalendarRules provide contracted court-rule content; counsel confirms results and resolves uncovered courts through source-cited manual review. InfoTrack and authorized courts provide filing/service networks and stamped results. Satchel owns orchestration, returned evidence and follow-up; provider outages or rejected filings remain open work. Health records and agent processing require the firm’s applicable data/health agreements, subprocessors and access policy before processing; implementing those agreements is part of delivery.

Microsoft 365/Word and Google Workspace remain editing and mail platforms; Box/Dropbox remain repositories. Satchel supplies integrated matter filing, versions, search and permissions, rather than rebuilding desktop Word or a general enterprise e-discovery hosting network. Matter evidence productions and source-cited drafts stay in scope. US tax and trust treatment is configured and reviewed by the firm’s lawyer/accountant; Satchel records calculation provenance and does not guarantee professional compliance by installation alone.

Matter-document originals remain limited to 1 MiB; intake-only R2 originals now support 10 MiB each. Resumable matter-file storage and quarantine remain missing.

OCR scanned records and index permitted document text, metadata and email with matter/date/type filters, exact page snippets and index freshness. Search applies matter walls before snippets and includes deletion of all derivatives on disposal.

Open matter DOCX files in Word through Microsoft 365, preserve tracked changes, comments and original versions, and save a new version back to the correct matter with conflict detection and access revocation.

DocuSign and Inkwell connectors request ordered or parallel signatures on an approved exact version, remind permitted recipients and retain signed bytes, certificate, provider ID and failure/decline history. Revoking a request never overwrites a signed original.

Microsoft 365/Outlook users file individual messages or approved threads and attachments to matters, retain sender/recipient headers and original .eml, associate sent replies and prevent duplicate filing across staff. Filing never grants a new matter reader.

Google Workspace/Gmail users select matter labels or messages for filing, preserve original headers, threads and attachments, associate outbound replies and handle deleted or revoked mail access without losing filed evidence.

Microsoft SharePoint/OneDrive and Google Drive connectors map selected folders and file versions to matters, track remote IDs and permission drift and offer controlled copy or linked-file custody. A revoked remote link is reported, never presented as a retained original.

Firms map existing Box and Dropbox folders to matters with least-privilege grants, version references, sync diagnostics and permission reconciliation; neither service becomes an alternative firm access boundary.

Staff install Satchel’s desktop drive for macOS and Windows, which shows only the matters they may access as folders in Finder or File Explorer, streams files on demand with optional per-matter offline pinning and opens them in any desktop application. Saving a file back records a new SAT-007 version with the saver’s identity and conflict detection, a file added to a matter folder is filed to that matter, and nothing is overwritten or deleted outside the matter’s retention and hold rules (FIRM-006). Ethical walls (FIRM-003), access removal and member deactivation take effect at the next sync and remove cached copies from the device; every open, save and offline pin is audited under FIRM-005.

Selected Google calendars exchange event creation, edits, cancellations, attendees and recurrence with stable IDs, loop prevention, conflict resolution and visible token/failure state; matter confidentiality controls event detail.

Microsoft 365/Outlook calendars support the same two-way lifecycle, delegated calendars and attendee changes, with subscription renewal, missed-change recovery and explicit choice of which details leave the matter.

fragments.text: The principal establishes a wall naming an active lawyer or principal custodian, who is always a wall member; for a wall INTAKE-010 creates at opening, the default custodian is the lawyer who records the restriction. After creation only the current custodian changes membership, hands custodianship to another active lawyer or principal inside the wall, or dissolves the wall, each with a recorded reason; nobody outside the wall, the principal and administrators included, adds themselves, changes members or custodian, approves access or dissolves it. With no active custodian the wall stays in force, reads "custodian unassigned", allows no exceptional access, and an active lawyer or principal inside the wall may take custodianship with a recorded reason. Exceptional access is requested with a reason by one active person in a native session (never an agent key, integration, portal user or client contact). Only the current custodian approves or refuses it, with a decision note. It lasts at most 60 minutes from approval and never renews: a further need is a new request. It is revoked early by the custodian or by any membership or custodian change. It opens the walled matter's current doors for that person only. It never confers membership or custodian authority, never reaches their agent keys or integrations, and never counts toward the every-wall permission for whole-firm archives, import originals or account aggregates. Request, decision, expiry, revocation and the recipient's walled reads under a grant are FIRM-005 audit actions readable inside the wall; the recipient sees their own request, decision and expiry. INTAKE-010's walled routing and the walls its restrictions create are proved under INTAKE-010.

Also (ct 22 Oct 2026): as the principal outside the wall, be refused adding yourself, changing members, re-designating the custodian, dissolving the wall and approving your own request; as an agent key and an integration, be refused requesting or using exceptional access. As the custodian, approve the principal's request, see it refused after 60 minutes, approve another and see it revoked by a membership change and again by handing custodianship to an inside lawyer. Under an active grant, be refused a whole-firm archive. Deactivate the custodian and see "custodian unassigned" with no grant possible until an inside lawyer takes custodianship. Evidence mapping: `tests/satchel/flows.test.mjs` — “ethical walls exclude a principal from current doors and require expiring audited custodian access” (principal creation; principal self-add, member change, custodian change, dissolution and self-approval refused; valid agent/integration credentials refused requesting/using grants; active person grant opens the matter but never whole-firm archives; no renewal; membership and inside-lawyer handover revoke grants; inactive custodian closes existing grants and new requests; inside counsel takes custody; reasoned dissolution/re-establishment; request/decision/read/expiry/revocation audit; restart/archive recovery). `tests/satchel/wall-expiry.mjs` is the separate real sixty-minute public-door journey: minute 1–59 reads succeed, read after minute 60 is refused, recipient expiry stays fixed, and one expiry action is audited; run on the exact candidate outside push Verify. `tests/satchel/contacts-journey.test.mjs` — “ethical wall creation, opaque conflict route, custodian decision and revocation” at 1440/390 (creation, opaque principal route, decision/trace, temporary access/revocation, inside handover, unassigned recovery, reasoned dissolution). `tests/satchel/trust.test.mjs` — “TRUST-001 reviewed source openings maintain separate bank, client/matter and operating records in exact cents; archives preserve approvals” (excluded balances). `tests/satchel/reminders.test.mjs` — “CAL-007 reassignment, quiet hours, acknowledgment and access revocation fence future sends without hiding delivery history” (recipient/queued-send exclusion).

fragments.text: **INTAKE-002 — Manage a lead pipeline.** **Status: done.** Assign two prospects, merge a duplicate with preserved provenance, miss a follow-up and inspect the owner’s due queue and conversion report. Evidence: `tests/satchel/leads.test.mjs` configures and renames stages (refusing an assistant); assigns two prospects (refusing a trust-officer assignee); flags a third lead as a duplicate by email. It confines assistants to their own leads, with no reassignment or merge, and refuses trust officers. It qualifies a lead, moves it and records the consultation outcome, refusing a stale revision. It merges the duplicate, keeping its source, referral and creator as provenance, and refuses later changes to the merged lead. The missed follow-up appears overdue and stalled in its owner’s due queue, and a lead due today joins the assistant’s queue. It refuses a lost lead without a reason and records one with a reason. It converts a lead only to a matter the person can see, one lead per matter. The conversion report checks exact counts by source and by stage, the stalled and lost reasons and the assistant’s narrower report, along with the audit records and the archive restore. Its historical native archive fixture proves the inclusive 14-day boundary through restore, pipeline, detail and report in America/New_York, including a UTC-midnight crossing, and proves that a missing action date alone is not stalled. Lead operations send no notification. `tests/satchel/leads-journey.test.mjs` adds stages and three leads at 1440 pixels (one assigned to the principal with a missed follow-up), merges the flagged duplicate, inspects the principal’s overdue due queue and stalled flag, converts the lead and reads the conversion report (50%; Google Ads 100%), then inspects the report at 390 pixels. Semantics: Staff record a lead with the prospect’s name, optional email and phone, inquiry summary and referral source; the referral source and creator are fixed provenance. Until INTAKE-001 forms ship, staff record leads by hand; each INTAKE-001 submission must become one of these leads before it ships. The principal and lawyers see and maintain every lead and configure the ordered pipeline stages; an assistant sees and works only leads assigned to them, records new leads assigned to themselves and cannot reassign or merge; trust officers see no leads. Assignees are active lawyers, assistants or the principal. A lead is qualified (pending, qualified or not qualified), moved between stages, and keeps a consultation outcome and a next action with an optional date. Each change is checked against the lead’s revision and appended to its immutable history. A possible duplicate is another open lead with the same email (case-insensitive), the same phone digits (at least seven) or the same name (ignoring case and spacing). Counsel merges a duplicate into a surviving lead: the survivor keeps its own fields, and the duplicate stays as a merged record with its source, referral, creator and history, shown as the survivor’s provenance. Losing a lead requires a reason. Converting links a matter opened through the conflict-reviewed door that the person can see, one lead per matter; INTAKE-007 adds full carry-over and MATTER-004’s opening trigger applies to that matter. Each person’s due queue lists their own open leads whose next-action date is on or before the firm-local today, flagged overdue when it is earlier. An open lead is stalled when its next action is overdue or when its last activity was 14 or more firm-local calendar days ago (inclusive). A missing next-action date alone is not stalled. Lead names and details never appear in notification subjects; INTAKE-001, INTAKE-007 and every future lead notification door inherit this rule before shipping. The conversion report excludes merged duplicates and counts leads, open, converted and lost leads by referral source and by stage, with conversion shown as converted ÷ leads in whole percent, rounded half-up. It lists stalled leads with their reasons and lost leads with their recorded reasons, and each person’s report covers only the leads they can see.

**TIME-001 — Run timers and timesheets.** **Status: done.** Start a timer on phone, resume on desktop, switch matters and submit the week; inspect one attributed entry per approved interval. Review a day of draft entries, edit durations and UTBMS codes, then Post day; inspect one attributed posted entry per accepted draft and exact daily hours/USD totals, with rejected drafts excluded and a repeated post producing no duplicate work. Evidence: `tests/satchel/timesheets.test.mjs` proves one running timer per person with visible switching, cross-session revision refusal, no access to unseen matters, one timer-sourced draft per closed interval dated in the firm timezone, posting refused while a timer runs, invalid UTBMS/minutes refused, edited durations and codes, a rejected draft, exact daily totals, Post day and Submit week each creating one attributed entry per accepted draft and nothing on repeat, posted drafts final, nonbillable entries refused on bills, per-person timesheets narrowed by current matter access, and archive restore. `tests/satchel/timesheets-journey.test.mjs` starts a timer at 390 pixels, resumes it in a 1440-pixel session, switches matters with the overlap notice, edits a draft’s duration and UTBMS codes, rejects another, sees the exact day total, posts the day and submits the week, then inspects the single billable and nonbillable entries. Semantics: Every staff member keeps only their own timers and timesheet, on matters they see. Timers live on the server, so one started on a phone resumes on a desktop. A person has at most one running timer: starting or resuming another pauses the running one in the same step and says so, so timers never overlap unnoticed. Each closed timer interval (pause, stop or switch) drafts exactly one entry attributed to its timekeeper: elapsed time rounded up to a whole minute (at most 1,440, longer intervals labeled for review), dated by the interval start in the firm timezone (UTC before firm setup), at the rate TIME-003 resolves for its work date (the firm default rate and increment when no agreement rule matches). The weekly timesheet runs Monday to Sunday; timekeepers add drafts and edit duration (1–1,440 minutes), billability and UTBMS task (letter plus three digits, e.g. L110) and activity (A plus three digits) codes, checked for format only until TIME-007 supplies firm code sets, or reject a draft. Post day or Submit week turns each remaining draft into one immutable entry, refused while the timekeeper has a running timer; rejected drafts are excluded, posted drafts are final and a repeated post records nothing. Daily and weekly totals show exact hours and minutes of non-rejected drafts and billable USD at TIME-003’s price (billed minutes, rounded up to the agreed increment, × hourly cents / 60, less any agreed discount, half-up to whole cents). Nonbillable entries are recorded but refused on bills. TIME-002 suggestions, TIME-003 rate schedules and TIME-007 code sets inherit these drafts and the posting rule before they ship.

Semantics: Agreement rules are append-only versions at firm, client (the matter’s recorded client name, exact match) or matter scope, optionally naming a timekeeper and a UTBMS task, each with an hourly USD-cents rate, a 1–60-minute rounding increment, a discount in basis points and a billable flag, effective from an inclusive date compared with the work date; a second rule with the same scope, timekeeper, task and date is refused. Precedence: a matter rule beats the client’s, which beats the firm’s; within one, a rule naming the timekeeper beats one that does not, then one naming the task, then the latest effective date on or before the work date; with no matching rule the FIRM-001 default rate and increment apply with no discount. Billed minutes are worked minutes rounded up to the increment; the charge is billed minutes × hourly cents × (10,000 − discount basis points) / 600,000, half-up to whole cents. A nonbillable rule makes matching work nonbillable (recorded, never billed). Timesheet drafts are priced from the agreement on their work date and posting freezes that price on the immutable entry, as does recording an entry without a rate; an explicit hourly rate on an entry or draft is recorded exactly as entered (SAT-004), with no increment or discount. Recorded entries keep their price when rules change, and issued bills keep their snapshot and exported bytes. Until FIRM-002 adds billing staff, the principal sets firm and client rules, and the principal or a lawyer who sees the matter sets matter rules and budgets. A matter budget is a versioned USD-cents amount with an alert percent; used is the recorded cents of every billable entry on the matter (time and disbursements). Each level alerts once per budget version, in the same step as the recording or budget change that crosses it: threshold when used × 100 ≥ budget × percent, exceeded when used > budget. Alerts are shown on the matter in Satchel and audited; no email is sent. TIME-002 suggestions, TIME-007 code sets and every later time-recording door or time import inherit this pricing and the budget check before they ship.

fragments.text: **TIME-004 — Bill flat and recurring fees.** **Status: done.** Create a monthly flat fee and a milestone fee, run the due schedule twice and inspect one draft per period with separate earned and trust balances. Evidence: `tests/satchel/fee-plans.test.mjs` runs the actual scheduled Worker twice across restart, then the due-fee API twice, and asserts exactly two monthly flat drafts, two recurring-retainer drafts and one milestone, zero draft earnings and unchanged $2,000 trust custody; unknown terms, unconfirmed events, future periods and uncompleted milestones are refused. It approves a completed monthly fee, authorizes and reconciles an exact $300 draw-down once, inspects $300 earned separately from the remaining $1,700 trust balance, refuses a prohibited milestone draw-down, and restores the complete fee plans, occurrences, earnings and balances. The same scheduled flow proves that an active owner's plan cannot supply a downgraded reviewer's authority, removed matter access stops that reviewer's plan, restored access prepares under that reviewer once, and voided occurrences stay single across restart and archive recovery. Its second public-door flow proves the $450 cap across $300 and $150 drafts, zero further fees, refused missing-plan billing, duplicate source, unauthorized exception and over-cap correction; a 17-minute blended line at $200.01/hour rounds to $56.67 despite its recorded $990/hour, and an explicitly permitted trial exception retains its separately reviewed $330 rate. Its third flow refuses missing nonhourly task/activity codes, independently reads an F fee with one unit and exact $300 in LEDES 1998B, XSD-validates XML flat charge F, approves a $50 courtesy correction, validates the $250 replacement and proves both original downloads remain unchanged. A blocked uncoded plan beside a valid coded plan on the same matter leaves the valid plan running and the blocked reason visible. The same flows refuse period-end earning on the final firm-local day, retain an exact $12.34 disbursement outside the time cap, restore a courtesy reduction up to the cap or original flat fee once, refuse one cent beyond either boundary, and preserve both prior XML exports. Assistant preparation and approval are refused. `tests/satchel/fee-plans-journey.test.mjs` uses the real billing screen at 1440 and 390 to review flat, milestone, capped and blended terms, replay the schedule without duplicate bills, inspect zero draft earnings and the reason for unknown earning eligibility, approve a completed monthly period and source-evidenced milestone, and inspect the earned values and retained terms without horizontal clipping. Semantics: The principal or a lawyer who sees the matter records immutable, explicitly reviewed fee terms: arrangement, USD cents, included work, permitted exceptions (or none), agreement reference, earning event and whether earned fees may be drawn from trust. Unknown earning or draw-down eligibility is refused with its reason. Flat, milestone and retainer arrangements create one nonhourly fee per due occurrence; once uses the reviewed start date, and monthly uses the first day of each calendar month from the reviewed start month through the inclusive final month. The first monthly date must be a month boundary. The scheduled Worker uses the firm IANA timezone and each plan reviewer's current authority and matter access, processing plans separately so a blocked plan cannot stop another plan on the same matter; counsel can also run the due schedule through a date. A unique plan/period identity survives restart and restore, including a voided occurrence, so replay never prepares another bill for it. Plans do not alter earlier drafts or invoices. Due processing only prepares drafts, earns zero, sends nothing and transfers nothing; failures remain visible with the missing guideline or other reason. Before approving a fee bill or its additive correction, counsel explicitly confirms the reviewed earning event and records source evidence; milestone earning also requires explicit completion, a future period cannot earn, and period-end earning is allowed only after the complete monthly period (or the once plan's end date) has passed in the firm timezone. Approval records the exact earned USD cents separately from trust custody. Prohibited draw-down is refused even for an earned bill; permitted draw-down still requires the existing same-matter, cleared-funds, officer and bank-result workflow, never inferred allocation or automatic movement. Capped and blended plans apply to selected recorded work within their inclusive date range, cannot overlap another capped/blended plan on the matter, and must be selected at preparation whenever selected time intersects that range. Caps cover time fees across all live drafts, approved invoices and additive corrections under that plan, with no monthly reset: chronological lines consume the remaining cap and can become zero; disbursements retain their exact amounts. Blended time uses worked whole minutes times the reviewed single hourly USD-cent rate divided by 60, rounded half-up to cents, independent of the original recorded hourly rate or increment. A permitted exception needs a separate counsel reference at preparation and uses the recorded entry amounts; no-exception plans refuse it. Positive corrections cannot exceed a reviewed cap or raise a flat, milestone, retainer or blended source above its originally reviewed line amount; a courtesy reduction can be restored only up to that amount. Source reservations and revision checks continue to prevent duplicate billing, and originals and terms remain immutable through corrections and archive recovery. Under a client LEDES guideline, nonhourly fees are F fee lines, one unit at the exact fee with the reviewed task/activity and timekeeper identity, never expenses or fabricated hours; all active-code, narrative and client guideline checks apply, XML 2.1.3 uses flat charge type F, and approval freezes both exports. TIME-005, TIME-008, BILL-001, BILL-004 and BILL-016 inherit these earning, cap, eligibility, source and nonhourly-code obligations before their new fee or bill doors ship.

fragments.text: **TIME-005 — Manage contingency and settlements.** **Status: partial.** Prepare a settlement with a lien reduction and expense recovery, compare all allocations to gross funds and refuse disbursement until approvals and cleared funds exist. CT policy ruling, 27 October 2026: APPROVE WITH RIDERS; TIME-005 remains PARTIAL. Native human counsel reviews the exact versioned contingency agreement, selected outcome, percentage basis, earning condition and completed earning evidence. Percentages use basis points and half-up USD-cent rounding. Referral allocations divide the counsel fee and never add a separate client charge; the restricted statement retains original obligations, reductions, source evidence and an exact reconciliation to gross recovery. Different counsel and designated trust-officer people approve each current exact statement by default. For a sole-practitioner firm, the native principal may explicitly enable a recorded separation waiver identifying its reason, scope, actor, effective version and time. Under that setting one currently authorized person may hold both capabilities but must record two distinct capacity approvals against the same revision. A replacement statement requires fresh approvals. The setting establishes product authority only and does not establish that a legal requirement is waivable. Current roles, officer designation, matter grants, ethical walls and cleared unreserved same-matter funds are rechecked at every applicable final action. Readiness neither reserves funds nor authorizes spending, recognizes revenue, issues an invoice or moves money. TIME-004 earning and eligibility controls and TIME-007 coding and guideline controls remain required before settlement fees enter billing. General audit retains attributable decision and revision metadata; settlement amounts and source documents remain restricted evidence. Archives retain history without restoring sessions or execution authority. CT remaining-proof inventory, preserved from the 27 October ruling: Remaining TIME-005 proof: preserve and complete the original settlement-to-disbursement acceptance; prove fractional-cent fee and referral rounding, reserved-fund exclusion, changed approver roles, officer designation and ethical walls, the recorded sole-practitioner setting, complete attributable audit, settlement-specific retention and erasure, restored-authority refusal and settlement-fee earning and coding integration. Bind the exact approved statement and each allocation into disbursement preparation and final approval, with current funds and authority rechecked. Record the clause’s own populated and refused screens at 1440 and 390 on the landed SHA; each UI acceptance test need assert its points at only one width. Native implementation evidence: `tests/satchel/fee-plans.test.mjs` — “Settlement statements reconcile recovery and refuse spending without current approvals and cleared funds” invokes settlementExecutionFlow in `tests/satchel/settlement-execution-flow.mjs` (fractional-cent fee and referral rounding, reserved-fund exclusion, exact payee and amount binding, changed roles, officer designation, grants, custom ceilings and walls, recorded sole-practitioner approval, attributed restricted audit and restored-authority refusal), settlementBillingFlow in `tests/satchel/settlement-billing-flow.mjs` (explicit earning and eligibility, active codes and guideline checks, immutable nonhourly LEDES, exact source and once-only charging, current authority at transfer approval and bank reconciliation, reciprocal double-spend refusal), and settlementRetentionFlow in `tests/satchel/settlement-retention-flow.mjs` (legal holds, principal-only expired disposal, preserved attribution, irreversible restricted-payload erasure and the older-archive fence). `tests/satchel/fee-plans-journey.test.mjs` — “Settlement workspace prepares recovery, records sole-practitioner settings and binds exact disbursements with approval and funds refusals at 1440 and 390” invokes settlementExecutionJourney in `tests/satchel/settlement-browser.mjs` through populated and refused settlement and firm-setting screens. Execution semantics: every trust disbursement on a settlement matter binds its current exact statement, allocation index, payee and amount; counsel and finance approvals are rechecked at preparation and final ledger posting. Full gross recovery must be covered by current cleared availability plus this statement’s own reserved or posted allocations; unrelated reservations remain excluded. Pending allocations must be declined before replacement, and a posted allocation keeps its original statement. A billed counsel fee and its generic counsel or referral disbursements cannot consume the same recovery twice. Settings changes require fresh capacity approvals. Archives retain policy and approval history, but a fresh installation stamp prevents restored history from supplying execution authority; restored settings require a new principal decision. Restricted text disposal follows the current expired matter retention schedule, refuses active holds and preserves identities and approval attribution; a retained settlement fee bill keeps its original source evidence and refuses disposal. Bank activity is recorded and reconciled through the existing trust doors; no provider execution or legal compliance is claimed. Fresh-judgment assertion map: `tests/satchel/fee-plans.test.mjs` — “Settlement statements reconcile recovery and refuse spending without current approvals and cleared funds”, lines 185–189 asserts all original obligations, reductions, net amounts and source references; lines 201–213 refuses pending replacement without changing terms, approvals or custody and permits replacement after decline; lines 215–226 asserts both attributable terms-review records and their archive preservation. `docs/evidence/time005-assertions.md` records the three formerly surviving mutations and their failing assertions. Implementation and assertion baseline: `7ff9b1c1905611d102131b5ec7681fee2b4cf3cb` (27 October 2026); the candidate changes only documentation and generated lock data from that baseline, with no production or test byte differing. The exact full candidate SHA and landing runs accompany the fresh ct judgment request. Native assertions are supplied for fresh ct judgment; no completion is counted. Gap: TRUST-004.

fragments.text: **TIME-007 — Code LEDES and UTBMS work.** **Status: done.** Prepare a coded insurer bill, reject a missing activity code, export valid LEDES 1998B and XSD-valid XML 2.1.3 and import a rejection to correct via a reviewed revision without duplicate charges. Evidence: `tests/satchel/ledes.test.mjs` has the principal (not a lawyer) configure task, activity and expense codes and a PT timekeeper ID, refuses an unknown code at the entry and timesheet doors once the firm has a set, records a Harbor Mutual guideline version, then refuses a five-line insurer bill naming a missing activity code, a missing timekeeper ID, a short and banned narrative, a rate over the PT maximum and an off-increment line, refuses a retired activity code, prepares the coded bill with a per-line activity code, approves it and checks the exported LEDES 1998B independently (header, 24 fields, [] terminators, dates, units × cost + adjustment, invoice total, the 10% discount as a −15.00 adjustment); outcome import is refused before export, for another invoice, an unknown line or a rejection without a reason, records the line-2 rejection once even when re-imported, refuses a correction to a retired code, prepares and approves a reviewed recode as invoice <n>-R1 with the same $810.00 total, refuses re-billing the corrected entry and a second branch, imports the R1 acceptance, keeps the original export byte-identical and the branch total at $810.00, and gives a client without a guideline a plain bill with no LEDES invoice. `tests/satchel/ledes-journey.test.mjs` adds a code and the guideline at 1440 pixels, sees preparation refused for the missing activity code, codes the line, approves and downloads the LEDES file, imports the rejection, prepares and approves the recode, downloads the -R1 replacement, then inspects the rejection, the replacement and the unchanged total at 390 pixels. Semantics: Until FIRM-002 adds billing staff, the principal configures the firm’s UTBMS code sets (task letter plus three digits, activity A plus three digits, expense E plus three digits; codes are retired, never deleted), each team member’s unique LEDES timekeeper ID and classification (PT, AS, OC, PL, LA or OT), and each client’s billing guideline. With no configured code of a kind, TIME-001’s format check is the whole rule; once a kind has codes, every entry, timesheet draft, bill coding and correction must use an active one. A guideline is an append-only version for the matter’s recorded client name (exact match, as TIME-003) naming the LEDES client ID and law-firm ID, whether task, activity and expense codes are required, a minimum narrative length, banned narrative phrases (case-insensitive), maximum hourly rates by classification and a required billing increment (0 for none); every fee line needs a timekeeper ID, and no LEDES field may contain | or []. A bill prepared for a client with a guideline is a LEDES bill: preparation checks every line against the current version and the firm code sets and refuses the whole bill naming each failing line and reason; codes may be chosen per line at preparation without changing the recorded entry. Before BILL-015 cutover, preparation reserves a unique invoice number (matter number, dash, the matter’s bill count including voided drafts; numbers are never reused) and approval freezes a LEDES 1998B file beside the reviewed CSV: YYYYMMDD dates, billing period from the earliest to the latest line date, units = billed hours to four decimals (half-up), unit cost = the hourly rate, and LINE_ITEM_ADJUSTMENT_AMOUNT carrying the agreed discount and rounding so the line total = units × unit cost (half-up to cents) + adjustment exactly; expenses are one unit at their amount. Downloading the frozen file marks the bill exported; bills for clients without a guideline stay plain reviewed bills. Counsel record the client’s e-billing outcome by importing its file (rows INVOICE_NUMBER|LINE_ITEM_NUMBER|STATUS|REASON, header optional, a blank line number meaning the whole invoice, a rejection needing its reason) only for that exported invoice; outcomes are append-only, labelled “imported from the e-billing file, not verified with the vendor” (Satchel never contacts the vendor), a re-imported file records nothing, and the invoice’s status follows its latest file (rejected if any row rejects). A rejected or wrong line is corrected through the existing reviewed correction branch: the correction may change the line’s codes, narrative or amount, is rechecked against the current guideline and code sets, and its LEDES file is a full replacement invoice numbered <original>-R<n> at every source’s current amount and coding, while Satchel’s ledger records only the additive delta, so no entry is charged twice and the original export is unchanged. BILL-001 batches, TIME-004/TIME-005 fee kinds, TIME-008 bulk entry and every later bill or time door inherit the code-set and guideline checks before they ship. The supported client-required XML profile is LEDES XML 2.1.3, validated in the public-door journeys against the unchanged [official LEDES Oversight Committee XSD](https://ledes.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/LEDES213xsd.zip) (`fixtures/ledes/Ledes213.xsd`; [format history](https://ledes.org/ledes-xml-ebilling-ver-2-1-format/)). The principal enables XML in an append-only guideline with explicit work country for invoice lines, firm vendor ID, the client-assigned firm vendor ID, client billing address/phone, firm billing-contact first/last name and email, and a client-assigned matter ID recorded separately for each matter; an expense-only invoice also names a configured billing timekeeper and its recorded hourly USD-cents rate for the required summary. Preparation checks the schema field lengths, XML characters, billed timekeeper names recorded as Last, First and IDs (at most 10 characters), and snapshots these details and the current US firm name/address/phone. Approval freezes a separate immutable XML artifact and digest; either download marks the bill exported and uses the same imported-outcome and reviewed-replacement flow. XML contains every fee and expense once, original line numbers as globally unique detail file-item numbers, USD, ISO dates, zero unrecorded tax and funds-applied amounts, exact matter/invoice totals, and the replacement reference in a standard extension. XML units are billed hours rounded half-up to two decimals as its XSD requires; base is the exact units × rate to four decimal dollar places, and a four-decimal signed line adjustment makes the exported line total equal the reviewed USD cents exactly (including discounts and rounding). XML does not claim vendor acceptance; settings changes and later replacements never rewrite either frozen export. Bills prepared without an XML profile retain their existing 1998B artifact; enabling the profile applies to future preparations and substantive reviewed corrections. XML evidence: `tests/satchel/ledes.test.mjs` validates the actual original, recoded replacement, fractional-unit adjustment and expense-only downloads with `xmllint` against the official XSD, independently reads identifiers, timekeepers, dates, codes and exact totals, refuses premature/assistant/revoked-access exports and incomplete XML profiles, proves settings changes and replacement exports leave original XML bytes unchanged, and refuses to borrow another matter’s client-assigned ID. `tests/satchel/ledes-journey.test.mjs` enters the XML profile through the guideline form, downloads and XSD-validates the original at 1440 pixels and the reviewed replacement at 390 pixels, checks the corrected activity and unchanged $420.00 invoice total, and inspects the saved XML details at both widths.

fragments.text: **TIME-008 — Submit bulk work and allocate revenue.** **Status: done.** Import a weekly timesheet with one invalid row, repair it, bill and partially collect; inspect attributed collections and commission calculations without changing original timekeeper records. Evidence: `tests/satchel/timesheets.test.mjs` — “TIME-001 cross-device timers never overlap, intervals draft one entry each, timesheets post a day or week once with exact totals” proves mixed weekly time and expense import, specific invalid-row refusal and repair, retained originals and original timekeeper separate from submitter, current attribution access, active UTBMS validation, expense receipt provenance, work-date pricing and approved cost snapshots, atomic once-only posting, changed-request refusal, restart and archive recovery. `tests/satchel/trust-transfer.test.mjs` — “Offline operating receipts allocate once, preserve credit, refuse unauthorized write-offs and release payments before an immutable void” proves explicit exact-version principal rule approval, source-linked partial collections and exact shares and commissions, independent write-offs and unapplied credit, applied credit, rule history, linked reversals and replay, principal-only economics including custodian audit refusal, current walls and archive recovery; its “TRUST-004 BILL-016 native payment/void guards / TRUST-005 inherited reconciliation: exact partial earned-fee reservations, distinct dual officers, interrupted bank reconciliation paired invoice payments and exact reviewed reversal post once” proves trust custody and pending bank applications excluded, cleared operating collections and once-only reversal, plus a taxed invoice with an explicit earned-work-only bank application, exact commission basis and archive recovery. `tests/satchel/providers.test.mjs` — “Hosted invoice collection allocates exact card and ACH funds once, preserves pending and returned states, and fences trust protection” proves paid operating sources, pending ACH and protected trust exclusion, and partial refunds before and after exact net-receipt allocation approval. `tests/satchel/timesheets-journey.test.mjs` — “TIME-001 timer started on a 390px phone, resumed and switched at 1440px, day reviewed with UTBMS codes and posted once”, continued by `tests/satchel/bulk-revenue-journey.mjs` function bulkRevenueJourney, proves the populated weekly import, invalid row, repair, reviewed post, agreement approval, billing, actual partial operating receipt, fee and expense and tax apportionment, attributed commissions and source-linked return at both 1440 and 390 pixels without changing original work records. Semantics: Bulk batches retain immutable originals, repaired inputs and normalized review snapshots. The principal may attribute work to eligible staff; other native timekeepers import their own work. Creator and original timekeeper remain separate, with current authority, original and current matter access, walls, pricing, codes, expense provenance and approved cost basis checked before atomic posting. Staff costs and compensation decisions remain principal-only. Allocation rules are explicit append-only principal approvals of the exact supporting document version and digest, agreement citation, origination and responsible-attorney shares, and commission basis points. Each allocation explicitly reviews an actual net operating collection and freezes its invoice components and rule version; receipt face value and unapplied credit are never substituted for invoice-applied cash. A cleared bank application retains its explicitly reviewed earned-work and tax split; only its earned-work component is apportioned across pre-tax source lines. Unsplit collected cents are apportioned across net invoice lines and tax by largest remainder with source-identity tie order. Only the fee portion is shared; expenses and tax remain distinct. Attorney shares and the firm remainder conserve every fee cent, and commissions round half-up from each share. Prior returns are excluded from the approved original; subsequent linked releases and reversals subtract successive calculations on that same frozen basis exactly once. Invoice value, unpaid balances, pending payments, trust custody and write-offs confer no commission. A bank-cleared operating application is distinct from its preceding trust custody. Rule changes never rewrite original work, cost snapshots, bills or earlier allocations. These are internal calculations and authorize no payout. `API.md` documents the public doors and exact semantics.

fragments.text: **CT policy ruling, 26 October 2026 — approved with riders; implementation status unchanged.** Staff cost entry, approval and version management, and economics reads and exports, require an active human native session whose current firm membership has the principal role. Initial principal authority comes from native firm setup; later grants and removals use the existing principal-controlled membership process and its audit. An administrator title, lawyer role, accountant role, manager title, custom role, agent sponsorship or provider account ownership does not confer this authority. Deactivation, role removal or session revocation ends access on the next request, including download requests. Historical approvals retain their original actor and time.

A principal enters an explicit hourly staff cost in exact USD cents for an identified timekeeper and effective work date, records its basis and approves the exact saved revision. The same principal may enter and approve it; independent second approval is not claimed. Draft or unapproved costs never enter profitability. Changes create append-only versions with author, approver, timestamps and effective dates; ambiguous overlapping approved versions are refused. Billing rates, invoices and later membership changes never supply or infer a staff cost. A retroactive approved version may change a newly generated calculation, but cannot rewrite an earlier exported artifact or its recorded basis.

Principals may inspect and export utilization, realization, collection rate, effective rate, billed and unbilled work, WIP, aging and matter profitability only within current matter permissions and ethical walls. Every metric discloses its formula, units, numerator, denominator, source identifiers, relevant revisions, filters, calculation time and supported as-of basis. Current-state results are labeled current-state; unsupported historical as-of requests are refused. Recorded-time utilization means billable recorded minutes divided by all recorded minutes in the same permitted cohort and period; it is not staff capacity, attendance or unrecorded work. A zero denominator yields unknown, not zero.

Profitability identifies the revenue basis and included staff costs and expenses. Every required time-cost component must have an applicable approved cost version. Otherwise the affected profitability is unknown, including any aggregate requiring that component; missing costs are never zero, inferred from billing prices or estimated as fact. An explicitly approved zero cost remains distinguishable from missing cost. Partial coverage may be shown separately with its coverage and exclusions, never labeled complete profitability. Pending payments, trust cash and earned revenue remain distinct. Voids, corrections, reversals and rebills retain source links and count their economic effect once.

Non-principals, agent keys, integrations, clients and payers receive neither staff cost records nor REPORT-002 economics through any read, search, count, drill, option, export or indirect response. FIRM-008 continues to own broader manager reporting scopes within built-in authority, grants and walls; it cannot widen this principal-only default. New economics doors inherit its server-door map before shipping.

An export is an explicit principal download, not external delivery. Authorization, current principal membership, matter access and walls are rechecked when generating and downloading it. Each export carries a confidential internal-use marking and a manifest identifying the firm, requesting actor, generation time, filters, supported as-of basis, formulas, source and cost-version basis, missing-data coverage and artifact hash. Custody is audited. Marking records custody and does not prevent copying. No public link or durable bearer authority is created. Staff costs, economics values, formula-basis payloads and their artifacts are excluded from email, SMS, portal summaries, webhooks, connected repositories, provider synchronization and agent or model context. This clause authorizes no sending, charging, payment approval or money movement.

Native archives preserve cost versions, approvals and export custody records under existing archive authorization and wall restrictions, without importing identities, sessions, credentials or authority grants. Restore validates integrity, retains imported history unchanged and appends a custody action; current authority is checked afresh. External effects remain paused under FIRM-007. Audit records cover cost entry, approval, supersession, export requests and outcomes, with immutable actor and revision evidence; unauthorized readers receive no cost payload through audit.

Applicable FIRM-006 holds block ordinary erasure and scheduled disposal. Approved disposal removes covered cost payloads and retained report derivatives or artifacts, records affected kinds and counts, and preserves only the permitted minimal audit and erasure evidence. Later erasure journals fence older archives against resurrection. Previously downloaded copies remain outside local erasure. Retention periods and lawful processing bases are firm decisions; this policy certifies neither compensation-law nor accounting compliance.

**Additional acceptance, without replacing the original journey:** Establish and remove principal authority through the existing membership process. Refuse direct economics, cost and download requests from every non-principal role, agent key and integration, including a manager with the widest permitted custom role. Remove principal authority between export generation and download and refuse the download. Demonstrate that wall-excluded rows, counts, options and aggregate contributions do not appear.
